#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.

```dart

The outer list literal `[truncatedToolCallTurn, scripted, scripted, scripted, scripted]` contains FOUR REFERENCES to the SAME inner list `scripted`. `FakeStreamFunction` calls `turns.removeAt(0)` on the OUTER list — that removes the reference from the outer list, not the inner list's contents. After EXHAUSTION, the final message is StopReason.error → `_settleAfterPrompt` first branch → not CodeMie, not over-window → `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply(error message)` → classifier: abortedOrError → false → return true → run finishes with the error → headless exit 1 ✓, interactive prints error line ✓.

What about a length-flagged empty that does NOT enter the hiccup path? Can that happen? In the loop, every empty (except error/aborted) is classified; length-flagged empty IS emptyAfterPartial → retried. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.

"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.
"""
8:# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
68:#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
70:#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
73:#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
87:#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
89:#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
90:#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
91:#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov

The shard machinery bin-packs new dirs at runtime, so the PR's claim "files verified bin-packed by shard_files.py" is plausible — test/agent and test/cli are directory units in the manifest presumably, so new files inside them run automatically. ✓

Now let me check `scripts/test_shards.json` quickly for test/agent and test/cli as units. Then verify the coverage gate — `crap4dart.yaml` mentions gates; the new file `empty_completion.dart` may be subject to coverage ratchets (`coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage`). New code + tests exist, so diff-coverage should be fine.

One more code-level check: the `Context` class — `context.messages` is mutable List? `_finishWithoutStream` does `context.messages.add(message)` — yes mutable. And `retryEmptyCompletion` passes `out` (context) to `classifyEmptyCompletion(out.messages, current)` — includes current as last ✓.

Now let me think about **whether the exhaustion error could re-trigger `_maybeOverWindowContinue`** — no (marker check).

**What about `_noteQuietMessageEnd`** — the ticket mentions it prints "(empty response: ...)" for empty messages. With retries, each empty retry emits the note? Check `_noteQuietMessageEnd` location — approval_commands.dart — it's called on MessageEnd for empty messages presumably. Cosmetic; multiple notes during a hiccup storm. Not a finding, maybe a suggestion? Skip.

**A REAL issue I should double-check — the IT-4 test's `expect(stream.calls, 5)`.** Wait: exhausted run interactive: truncatedToolCallTurn(1) + 4 empties = 5 calls. Then the user types "try again please" → the NEXT turn: the fake stream's turns list is EXHAUSTED (6th scripted turn is `textTurn('fresh answer after the user re-asked')` — yes there are 6 entries). calls >= 6 ✓. OK.

**IT-4 flakiness**: poll loop `for 400 × 25ms` = 10s cap. With real backoff 3.5s, fine. On slow CI, 10s budget ok.

**Now — `classifyEmptyCompletion` being called by BOTH the loop (with `out.messages` = loop context) and the CLI settle (with `_agent.state.messages`)**. Subtle: after the loop settles an exhaustion ERROR message (empty content, stopReason error), the CLI's `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply` classifies → abortedOrError → no nudge ✓.

But what about this: clean-empty settle in the CLI. Turn: user msg + empty(stop) → loop: cleanEmpty (budget 0) → break → CLI nudges 'continue' (isAutoContinue: true). The nudged run streams... suppose it returns a REAL answer. ✓ REG-1 test pins this ✓.

Now suppose the nudged run ALSO returns empty: loop again cleanEmpty → break → `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply`: `_emptyReplyNudgesLeft` is now 0 → false → settle → exit 0 with an empty final. That's the pinned AC2 behavior ("empty → nudge → empty settles"). The ticket's invariant 1 contradicts, but AC2/REG-1 pin it — declared deviation, noted.

**Another check — `retryEmptyCompletion` is called via `_retryDegenerateEmpty` for EVERY assistant message (healthy ones too).** Overhead: `classifyEmptyCompletion` on every completion — O(turn) scan only when the message is empty (notEmpty → early return before the scan) ✓ cheap.

**StopReason.length non-empty messages** — classify → notEmpty → break ✓ (truncation with content keeps existing path: `_failToolCallsFromTruncatedMessage` etc. — wait, does the length+content path still terminate the run? `_terminalRunMessages` returns null for length; the tool phase fails the truncated tool calls, hasMore false → settle... that's pre-existing behavior, unchanged).

Hmm wait — actually now I want to check one more edge: **empty message with stopReason == toolUse** (provider said toolUse but no tool calls arrived). isEmpty → true; not error/aborted; truncation signal? toolUse != length, != stop → false; turn scan → if partial content → emptyAfterPartial (retry) else cleanEmpty. Fine.

**`emptyHiccupRetries` semantics vs `maxEmptyRetries` on the Flutter app host**: app host (flutter_app? packages?) uses AgentLoopConfig default maxEmptyRetries=1. Now empty-after-partial in the app: 1 generic retry + 3 hiccup retries w/ backoff then ERROR instead of settling. The app host might surface the error — behavior change for app users: previously 1 retry then settle empty (weird UX but not exit-code relevant); now up to 4 retries + error. That IS the intended fix (the loop is shared). ✓

**Doc comment on `AgentLoopConfig.emptyHiccupRetries`: "`0` restores the legacy accept-empty settle."** — traced earlier as wrong: with 0, empty-after-partial → exhaustion error (CLI) or 1 generic retry then error (app). The "legacy accept-empty settle" is NOT restored. Misleading public doc — IMPORTANT.

Hmm wait, let me re-trace for the APP host with emptyHiccupRetries=0, maxEmptyRetries=1 (default): 
- iter1: verdict emptyAfterPartial; generic(0) < 1 → generic=1; re-stream (no backoff).
- iter2: still emptyAfterPartial; generic(1) not < 1; not cleanEmpty; hiccup(0) >= 0 → EXHAUSTION error.
So no settle. For legacy to be restored you'd need... nothing restores it. The doc is wrong. Unless "restores the legacy accept-empty settle" means for cleanEmpty... no, cleanEmpty breaks anyway. Confirmed: doc bug.

Also — **`maxEmptyRetries` interplay subtle change**: legacy `_retryDegenerateEmpty` for the APP host retried ANY degenerate empty up to 1 and then SETTLED it (accept-empty). NEW: after the generic budget, a still-empty message now goes down the HICCUP path if the turn had partial content → 3 more retries → error. So app hosts get behavior change beyond the new knob: that's the intent (gh-1577 is about the loop), fine — but note `maxEmptyRetries`'s own doc ("a blank answer never ends a run on the first try") still accurate.

Now — **the biggest remaining question: `retryEmptyCompletion` breaks on cleanEmpty only when generic budget is EXHAUSTED.** For the CLI (maxEmptyRetries=0) cleanEmpty breaks immediately ✓. For the app host, first cleanEmpty costs 1 generic retry ✓ legacy. BUT: **the generic budget is consumed by hiccup retries FIRST if the message is emptyAfterPartial at iter1.** Sequence for app host: partial → empty1 (emptyAfterPartial): generic=1, re-stream → empty2 (emptyAfterPartial): hiccup path ×3 → error. Total 5 attempts. Fine, bounded.

**One more possible bug — the exhaustion error message and `lastStopReason` when current is the ERROR terminal from a provider error mid-retry?** abortedOrError breaks before exhaustion; fine.

**CancelToken reopened (issue #1126 mechanism)** — `reopen()` exists; irrelevant.

**Thread-safety/reentrancy** — single loop, fine.

Now let me verify the claimed behavior for the **interactive note**: `_noteQuietMessageEnd` — let me look at it to make sure the hiccup path doesn't ALSO print the quiet note before the error (cosmetic duplication). Actually skip — cosmetic.

**Let me now check `test_shards.json` includes test/agent and test/cli** (so the new files really run in CI):

{"command":"grep -n \"\\\"test/agent\\\"\\|\\\"test/cli\\\"\\|test/agent\\|test/cli\" scripts/test_shards.json | head -5; ls test/agent/ | head; grep -rn \"empty_completion\\|hiccup\" scripts/test_shards.json | head -3"}
{"command":"grep -n \"_noteQuietMessageEnd\" lib/src/cli/*.dart | head -5"}

blocks.text:
The bin-pack confirms both new test files (`test/agent/empty_completion_test.dart` and `test/cli/agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart`) are bin-packed across the 4 shards at runtime (grep count = 2 = the two files present across shard outputs). ✓ The PR's shard claim checks out.

Now let me finish the remaining verification items:

1. Check `_noteQuietMessageEnd` interplay (cosmetic).
2. Confirm `pubspec` version/changelog handling — does this repo require a CHANGELOG entry per PR? Looking at the repo there's CHANGELOG.md maintained by tooling probably. The PR has no changelog change — check whether AGENTS.md requires it. Probably auto-generated from gh issues. Skip.
3. Verify the `flutter_agent_harness.dart` export ordering convention — exports seem alphabetical-ish: agent.dart, agent_loop.dart, agent_tool.dart, then `empty_completion.dart` inserted after agent_tool.dart and before misuse_breaker.dart — alphabetical ✓ (e < m).
4. One more correctness review of the loop: **`_retryDegenerateEmpty` doc comment now says "bounded by `config.maxEmptyRetries`" but the function delegates to retryEmptyCompletion which uses BOTH budgets** — the doc at line ~1404-1408 was updated to mention the part file ✓.

5. **Check `Context` import in empty_completion.dart**: imports `../context.dart` and `../types.dart` — pure ✓.

6. **Potential DOUBLE exhaustion-message when the loop is re-entered after steering?** The exhaustion breaks the inner loop and `_terminalRunMessages` returns terminal → run ends. ✓

7. **What about `pollSteering` after exhaustion?** Terminal returns before. ✓

8. **Dead code check**: `_retryDegenerateEmpty` is now a pure delegation wrapper — could be inlined at the single call site (line 1139). Minor duplication/wrapper — SUGGESTION-level (keep or inline; the wrapper preserves the legacy name/doc). Fine as-is honestly; maybe not worth a comment. I'll fold into a suggestion about the public API surface.

9. **IT-4 test poll loop: `calls = stream.calls` assigned but unused variable warning?** `int calls = 0; calls = stream.calls; if (calls >= 5 ...)` — it IS used in the condition ✓. But the second poll loop doesn't assign `calls` — fine.

10. **`emptyHiccupExhaustedError` says "repeat or rephrase the request"** — good UX for headless hosts.

11. Check `test/integration` exclusion doesn't matter here.

12. One more potential issue — **`classifyEmptyCompletion(_agent.state.messages, lastMessage)` in `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply`: `_agent.state.messages` is `List<Message>` unmodifiable view?** It compiles, fine.

13. **Does `_agent.state.messages` include the CURRENT (last) message at settle time?** `_settleAfterPrompt(lastMessage)` — called from `_afterRun` presumably with `state.messages.lastOrNull`. The `identical` skip handles presence; if the message is present it's skipped; then the scan walks the REST of the turn — for a clean empty: user message → break → false-ish → cleanEmpty ✓ nudge fires as before. ✓ REG-1 CLI test passes, confirming.

14. **Behavior change alert for the CLI**: legacy `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply` ALSO nudged on: empty after partial text (verdict now emptyAfterPartial → no nudge). In the CLI the loop now handles those (retry/error). ✓ consistent. And empty after `StopReason.length` on the LAST message (truncation) — legacy nudged; now: if the final message is length-flagged EMPTY it never escapes the loop (retried to error) — except the E5 cancel race. ✓ consistent modulo the race.

Now I understand the changes well. Let me analyze for potential issues:

### Issue analysis

1. **`retryEmptyCompletion` classification with `out.messages` vs `current`**:
   - `_streamAssistantResponse` returns `(finished, context)` — note: does `_consumeResponseStream` add the message to `context.messages`? Let me check. The classifier docs say "both call sites pass the live transcript ending in it", and it uses `identical(entry, message)` to skip it. But wait — in `retryEmptyCompletion`, after a retry `_streamAssistantResponse(out, ...)` returns `(current, out)` — where `out` is the context. If `_consumeResponseStream` appends the partial/finished message to `context.messages`, then `out.messages.last == current` (identical). But on exhaustion, `_finishWithoutStream(out, emit, _terminalMessage(...))` is called WITHOUT `replaceLast: true` — this ADDS a new terminal message to `context.messages` even though the empty completion is already in there? Let me check: in `retryEmptyCompletion`, at exhaustion, `current` is the last empty message which IS in `out.messages` (appended by the stream consume). Then `_finishWithoutStream` with default `replaceLast: false` APPENDS the error message. So transcript will have: empty message, then terminal error message. Is that intended? In the aborted path at line 1674, `_finishWithoutStream(context, emit, _terminalMessage(config.model, StopReason.aborted, 'Operation aborted'))` — also appends. So this matches the existing abort pattern. OK.

   But wait — there's a subtle issue in `_turnCarriesPartialContent` after the FIRST retry stream: `_streamAssistantResponse` appends the streamed (empty) message into `context.messages`? Let me verify `_consumeResponseStream` to see if the finished message is appended to context.messages.

   Actually, look at line ~1500: `return (finished, context);` — and in the no-terminal-event path, `_finishWithoutStream(context, emit, ..., replaceLast: streamed.addedPartial)`. So `_consumeResponseStream` adds the partial to context.messages as it streams ("keeping the partial message in [context.messages]"). So after each `_streamAssistantResponse`, the streamed message IS the last element of `context.messages`. And `identical(entry, message)` skips exactly that one. Good.

   However — hmm, one subtlety: on the SECOND iteration of the loop, `out.messages` now ends with the FIRST empty message (from the previous attempt). The classifier's scan walks `turnHistory.reversed`, skipping `current` (the new empty), then encounters the PREVIOUS empty assistant message. `isEmptyAssistantCompletion(prev)` is true and `_carriesTruncationSignal(prev)` is false → continues the scan. Then it reaches the original partial content → true. Fine. The previous empties don't count as "partial content" but the original partial text does. Good — the retry counting is driven by the `hiccup` counter anyway.

2. **Backoff bug?** `emptyHiccupBackoffFor(attempt: hiccup, ...)` — the delay happens BEFORE incrementing `hiccup`, and before re-streaming. First retry delay: baseDelay * 2^0 = 500ms. Second: 1s, third: 2s. Fine.

   `attempt.clamp(0, 20)` — `1 << 20` = 1048576 * 500ms ≈ way over the 8s cap, fine. But there's an int overflow consideration: 500ms << 20 is fine.

3. **`emptyHiccupRetries: 0` "restores the legacy accept-empty settle"?** Per the doc comment on the config: "Default: 3. `0` restores the legacy accept-empty settle." Let's trace `emptyHiccupRetries: 0` with an `emptyAfterPartial` message: 
   - verdict = emptyAfterPartial.
   - `generic < config.maxEmptyRetries`? For the app host default maxEmptyRetries = 1: generic=0 < 1 → generic=1, re-stream. Next iteration: emptyAfterPartial again, generic=1 not < 1. Not cleanEmpty. `hiccup >= 0` → exhaustion → error. Hmm — so `emptyHiccupRetries: 0` doesn't exactly "restore the legacy accept-empty settle"; it converts an empty-after-partial into a loud error after spending the generic budget. For CLI (`maxEmptyRetries: 0`): first iteration: generic=0 not < 0, not cleanEmpty, hiccup=0 >= 0 → immediate exhaustion error. So with `emptyHiccupRetries: 0` the run errors out instead of "accept-empty settle". The doc comment says "0 restores the legacy accept-empty settle" — that's inaccurate. But is this a big deal? It's a doc comment inaccuracy — the behavior with 0 is arguably BETTER (loud error, per ticket intent: never silent exit 0). Actually wait — the ticket says headless exit 0 requires content. A silent settle of an empty-after-partial would be exactly the bug. So the doc comment is misleading rather than the behavior wrong. That's a SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT-level doc issue.

   Hmm, actually let me think about whether "0 restores the legacy accept-empty settle" is describing the cleanEmpty path: with `maxEmptyRetries` and `emptyHiccupRetries = 0`... no. Let me re-read: "Default: 3. `0` restores the legacy accept-empty settle." The legacy behavior for empty-after-partial in the app host: `_isDegenerateEmpty` true → retry up to maxEmptyRetries (1) → still empty → settle as stop. So with emptyHiccupRetries=0 and maxEmptyRetries=1: generic retry 1 fires, then next empty: generic not < 1, not cleanEmpty, hiccup 0 >= 0 → ERROR. So no, it doesn't restore legacy settle. Doc inaccuracy confirmed.

4. **The `attempts` count in the exhaustion message**: `attempts: 1 + generic + hiccup`. Hmm. When CLI wires `maxEmptyRetries: 0`, generic stays 0, hiccup reaches 3: attempts = 1 + 0 + 3 = 4. Total requests: original + 3 retries = 4. OK. Test IT-2 says "partial + 4 empties (1 + 3 retries) = 5 requests" and `expect(stream.calls, 5)`. Hmm wait — `truncatedToolCallTurn` is request 1, then 4 empties = requests 2-5. So calls=5: 1 truncated + 1 original empty + 3 retries = 5. attempts for empties = 4 = 1 + 0 + 3. OK consistent.

   But hold on: when does the FIRST hiccup retry happen? Trace with maxEmptyRetries=0 (CLI): iteration 1: verdict=emptyAfterPartial; generic(0) < maxEmptyRetries(0)? No. cleanEmpty? No. hiccup(0) >= emptyHiccupRetries(3)? No. → else branch: backoff 500ms, hiccup=1; re-stream → empty. Iteration 2: hiccup(1)>=3? No → backoff 1s, hiccup=2, re-stream → empty. Iteration 3: backoff 2s, hiccup=3, re-stream → empty. Iteration 4: hiccup(3) >= 3 → exhaustion. Total empties: 4 (1 initial + 3 retries). Total requests 5. ✓.

5. **Mixed-budget sequencing concern**: the `generic` budget is consumed BEFORE `cleanEmpty` break. With app-host default (maxEmptyRetries=1, emptyHiccupRetries=3) and a CLEAN empty: iteration 1: verdict=cleanEmpty; generic 0 < 1 → generic=1, re-stream (no backoff). Suppose the retry is also cleanEmpty: generic 1 not < 1 → cleanEmpty → break. So clean empty gets 1 silent retry in the loop (legacy behavior preserved), then the CLI nudge. Legacy `_retryDegenerateEmpty` did exactly this (retry while degenerate && retries < maxEmptyRetries). ✓ REG-1 preserved for the host.

   Now for the CLI (`maxEmptyRetries: 0`): cleanEmpty → generic 0 not < 0 → cleanEmpty → break immediately. Legacy with maxEmptyRetries=0: while loop never entered → break. ✓ same.

   And emptyAfterPartial in the CLI: retried with backoff (new). ✓.

   But NOW: consider an emptyAfterPartial in the APP HOST (maxEmptyRetries=1): iteration 1: generic 0 < 1 → generic=1, re-stream immediately (NO backoff — the generic retry has no delay, matching legacy). Suppose still emptyAfterPartial: generic not < 1, not cleanEmpty, hiccup 0 < 3 → backoff 500ms, hiccup=1, retry... So the hiccup budget adds 3 MORE retries after the generic one. Total attempts = 1 + 1 + 3 = 5. Bounded. Fine.

6. **`_turnCarriesPartialContent` treats ANY `ToolResultMessage` in the turn as partial content.** Hmm — think about this scenario: user asks something; model returns tool call; tool executes (ToolResultMessage appended); next completion is empty → classified emptyAfterPartial → up to 3 retries with backoff, then error if still empty. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.
"""

**A REAL issue I should double-check — the IT-4 test's `expect(stream.calls, 5)`.** Wait: exhausted run interactive: truncatedToolCallTurn(1) + 4 empties = 5 calls. Then the user types "try again please" → the NEXT turn: the fake stream's turns list is EXHAUSTED (6th scripted turn is `textTurn('fresh answer after the user re-asked')` — yes there are 6 entries). calls >= 6 ✓. OK.

**IT-4 flakiness**: poll loop `for 400 × 25ms` = 10s cap. With real backoff 3.5s, fine. On slow CI, 10s budget ok.

**Now — `classifyEmptyCompletion` being called by BOTH the loop (with `out.messages` = loop context) and the CLI settle (with `_agent.state.messages`)**. Subtle: after the loop settles an exhaustion ERROR message (empty content, stopReason error), the CLI's `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply` classifies → abortedOrError → no nudge ✓.

But what about this: clean-empty settle in the CLI. Turn: user msg + empty(stop) → loop: cleanEmpty (budget 0) → break → CLI nudges 'continue' (isAutoContinue: true). The nudged run streams... suppose it returns a REAL answer. ✓ REG-1 test pins this ✓.

Now suppose the nudged run ALSO returns empty: loop again cleanEmpty → break → `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply`: `_emptyReplyNudgesLeft` is now 0 → false → settle → exit 0 with an empty final. That's the pinned AC2 behavior ("empty → nudge → empty settles"). The ticket's invariant 1 contradicts, but AC2/REG-1 pin it — declared deviation, noted.

**Another check — `retryEmptyCompletion` is called via `_retryDegenerateEmpty` for EVERY assistant message (healthy ones too).** Overhead: `classifyEmptyCompletion` on every completion — O(turn) scan only when the message is empty (notEmpty → early return before the scan) ✓ cheap.

**StopReason.length non-empty messages** — classify → notEmpty → break ✓ (truncation with content keeps existing path: `_failToolCallsFromTruncatedMessage` etc. — wait, does the length+content path still terminate the run? `_terminalRunMessages` returns null for length; the tool phase fails the truncated tool calls, hasMore false → settle... that's pre-existing behavior, unchanged).

Hmm wait — actually now I want to check one more edge: **empty message with stopReason == toolUse** (provider said toolUse but no tool calls arrived). isEmpty → true; not error/aborted; truncation signal? toolUse != length, != stop → false; turn scan → if partial content → emptyAfterPartial (retry) else cleanEmpty. Fine.

**`emptyHiccupRetries` semantics vs `maxEmptyRetries` on the Flutter app host**: app host (flutter_app? packages?) uses AgentLoopConfig default maxEmptyRetries=1. Now empty-after-partial in the app: 1 generic retry + 3 hiccup retries w/ backoff then ERROR instead of settling. The app host might surface the error — behavior change for app users: previously 1 retry then settle empty (weird UX but not exit-code relevant); now up to 4 retries + error. That IS the intended fix (the loop is shared). ✓

**Doc comment on `AgentLoopConfig.emptyHiccupRetries`: "`0` restores the legacy accept-empty settle."** — traced earlier as wrong: with 0, empty-after-partial → exhaustion error (CLI) or 1 generic retry then error (app). The "legacy accept-empty settle" is NOT restored. Misleading public doc — IMPORTANT.

Hmm wait, let me re-trace for the APP host with emptyHiccupRetries=0, maxEmptyRetries=1 (default): 
- iter1: verdict emptyAfterPartial; generic(0) < 1 → generic=1; re-stream (no backoff).
- iter2: still emptyAfterPartial; generic(1) not < 1; not cleanEmpty; hiccup(0) >= 0 → EXHAUSTION error.
So no settle. For legacy to be restored you'd need... nothing restores it. The doc is wrong. Unless "restores the legacy accept-empty settle" means for cleanEmpty... no, cleanEmpty breaks anyway. Confirmed: doc bug.

Also — **`maxEmptyRetries` interplay subtle change**: legacy `_retryDegenerateEmpty` for the APP host retried ANY degenerate empty up to 1 and then SETTLED it (accept-empty). NEW: after the generic budget, a still-empty message now goes down the HICCUP path if the turn had partial content → 3 more retries → error. So app hosts get behavior change beyond the new knob: that's the intent (gh-1577 is about the loop), fine — but note `maxEmptyRetries`'s own doc ("a blank answer never ends a run on the first try") still accurate.

Now — **the biggest remaining question: `retryEmptyCompletion` breaks on cleanEmpty only when generic budget is EXHAUSTED.** For the CLI (maxEmptyRetries=0) cleanEmpty breaks immediately ✓. For the app host, first cleanEmpty costs 1 generic retry ✓ legacy. BUT: **the generic budget is consumed by hiccup retries FIRST if the message is emptyAfterPartial at iter1.** Sequence for app host: partial → empty1 (emptyAfterPartial): generic=1, re-stream → empty2 (emptyAfterPartial): hiccup path ×3 → error. Total 5 attempts. Fine, bounded.

**One more possible bug — the exhaustion error message and `lastStopReason` when current is the ERROR terminal from a provider error mid-retry?** abortedOrError breaks before exhaustion; fine.

**Thread-safety/reentrancy** — single loop, fine.

blocks.text:
The bin-pack confirms both new test files (`test/agent/empty_completion_test.dart` and `test/cli/agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart`) are bin-packed across the 4 shards at runtime (grep count = 2 = the two files present across shard outputs). ✓ The PR's shard claim checks out.

Now let me finish the remaining verification items:

1. Check `_noteQuietMessageEnd` interplay (cosmetic).
2. Confirm `pubspec` version/changelog handling — does this repo require a CHANGELOG entry per PR? Looking at the repo there's CHANGELOG.md maintained by tooling probably. The PR has no changelog change — check whether AGENTS.md requires it. Probably auto-generated from gh issues. Skip.
3. Verify the `flutter_agent_harness.dart` export ordering convention — exports seem alphabetical-ish: agent.dart, agent_loop.dart, agent_tool.dart, then `empty_completion.dart` inserted after agent_tool.dart and before misuse_breaker.dart — alphabetical ✓ (e < m).
4. One more correctness review of the loop: **`_retryDegenerateEmpty` doc comment now says "bounded by `config.maxEmptyRetries`" but the function delegates to retryEmptyCompletion which uses BOTH budgets** — the doc at line ~1404-1408 was updated to mention the part file ✓.

5. **Check `Context` import in empty_completion.dart**: imports `../context.dart` and `../types.dart` — pure ✓.

6. **Potential DOUBLE exhaustion-message when the loop is re-entered after steering?** The exhaustion breaks the inner loop and `_terminalRunMessages` returns terminal → run ends. ✓

7. **What about `pollSteering` after exhaustion?** Terminal returns before. ✓

8. **Dead code check**: `_retryDegenerateEmpty` is now a pure delegation wrapper — could be inlined at the single call site (line 1139). Minor duplication/wrapper — SUGGESTION-level (keep or inline; the wrapper preserves the legacy name/doc). Fine as-is honestly; maybe not worth a comment. I'll fold into a suggestion about the public API surface.

9. **IT-4 test poll loop: `calls = stream.calls` assigned but unused variable warning?** `int calls = 0; calls = stream.calls; if (calls >= 5 ...)` — it IS used in the condition ✓. But the second poll loop doesn't assign `calls` — fine.

10. **`emptyHiccupExhaustedError` says "repeat or rephrase the request"** — good UX for headless hosts.

11. Check `test/integration` exclusion doesn't matter here.

12. One more potential issue — **`classifyEmptyCompletion(_agent.state.messages, lastMessage)` in `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply`: `_agent.state.messages` is `List<Message>` unmodifiable view?** It compiles, fine.

13. **Does `_agent.state.messages` include the CURRENT (last) message at settle time?** `_settleAfterPrompt(lastMessage)` — called from `_afterRun` presumably with `state.messages.lastOrNull`. The `identical` skip handles presence; if the message is present it's skipped; then the scan walks the REST of the turn — for a clean empty: user message → break → false-ish → cleanEmpty ✓ nudge fires as before. ✓ REG-1 CLI test passes, confirming.

14. **Behavior change alert for the CLI**: legacy `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply` ALSO nudged on: empty after partial text (verdict now emptyAfterPartial → no nudge). In the CLI the loop now handles those (retry/error). ✓ consistent. And empty after `StopReason.length` on the LAST message (truncation) — legacy nudged; now: if the final message is length-flagged EMPTY it never escapes the loop (retried to error) — except the E5 cancel race. ✓ consistent modulo the race.

15. Let me double check the **E5 race severity** by re-reading the exact code once more:

```dart
while (!cancelled) {
  verdict = classify(...)
  ... (retry/backoff/exhaustion decisions)
  (current, out) = await _streamAssistantResponse(out, ...);
  cancelled = _isCancelRequested(cancelToken);
}
if (cancelled && _isDegenerateEmpty(current)) {
  current = aborted terminal
}
```

Case: cancel fires during the LAST retry request; provider returns a length-flagged EMPTY (or silent-truncation-flagged empty). Loop exits (cancelled). `_isDegenerateEmpty(current)` → stopReason is `length` (not `stop`) → false → return length-empty. Run settles the turn normally → TurnEnd(stopReason: length) → headless exit 0. The user pressed abort but gets exit 0 and a silently-empty turn. E2 says the run settles aborted (exit 130). This is a genuine, if narrow, contract violation. Fix is trivial: `if (cancelled && isEmptyAssistantCompletion(current))` or use the classifier verdict != notEmpty/abortedOrError. IMPORTANT.

Hmm — wait, actually also consider cancel fires during a retry request and the provider returns a NON-empty partial (text). Then current is notEmpty → returned → run continues tool phase → settles normally with content. Exit 0 with real content — acceptable (the abort lost the race to a real completion; the CLI surfaces the abort UX separately... actually does it? If the user aborted but the run completed with content, the CLI... there's `_runAbortRequested` sticky marker handling in compaction paths. For the plain run path, hmm. That's pre-existing behavior for abort-during-stream though — NOT introduced by this PR. Only the empty-variant escape is newly reachable via this PR's retry loop (previously `_retryDegenerateEmpty` never re-streamed for CLI (budget 0) and the loop-level cancel short-circuit `_abortedTurn` handled the next turn). Actually pre-existing: cancel during the LAST turn's stream, provider returns clean-stop EMPTY → old `_retryDegenerateEmpty`: `!(cancelToken?.isCancelled ?? false)` → loop not entered → empty returned → settle → CLI nudge? `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply` (old): stop, empty → nudge ONCE → nudged run: `_streamAssistantResponse` short-circuits via `_isCancelRequested` at top → `_abortedTurn` → terminal aborted → exit 130. So OLD code recovered the abort via the nudge path (accidentally). NEW code: clean-stop empty + cancelled → E5 converts to aborted ✓ same. Length-flagged empty + cancelled → escapes → exit 0 (old code: length-flagged EMPTY → old `_isDegenerateEmpty` false (not stop) → no retry → settle; old nudge: `stopReason != error && != aborted` → length passes → `_assistantMessageIsEmpty` → nudge → abort short-circuit → 130). So the NEW code REGRESSES the length-flagged-empty+cancel case from 130 to 0! The old accidental recovery via the nudge is gone because `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply` now requires cleanEmpty. This strengthens the finding: it's a real regression scenario vs main, though it requires the abort race. Keep IMPORTANT (race-window). Could argue BLOCKING? It contradicts the PR's own headline contract ("never a silent exit 0") in a narrow race. Given severity guidance ("when in doubt, start one level higher"), hmm. The window is milliseconds-to-seconds wide (cancel can land any time during the final request OR during backoff). For headless harness runs with session deadlines, deadline-aborts landing in this window would convert an aborted run into exit 0 — exactly the class of lie this ticket is about. But the final turn WOULD contain a length-flagged empty with zero content — invariant 1 violation ("headless exit 0 requires at least one non-empty assistant message or executed tool call in the run's final turn") — the final turn here = [tool-call assistant msg, tool result, length-empty]. Hmm, there WAS an executed tool call in the turn... invariant satisfied technically. Ugh, borderline. The verdict rules: BLOCKING = correctness/bug findings. It IS a correctness bug (abort → exit 0 regression vs main), though narrow. The machine cross-checks blocking count vs inline comments. I'll be honest: I rate it IMPORTANT rather than BLOCKING because it needs a precise race (cancel landing during the final retry request AND the provider returning a truncation-flagged empty rather than a clean stop or content) — probability low, and the run DID do real work in the turn. But per "when in doubt, start one level higher"... let me think about the actual impact: exit 0 instead of 130 for an aborted run. Harnesses relying on exit codes would treat an aborted run as success — the exact gh-1577 failure class (false success). The deadline case (E7-adjacent): session deadline fires → cance…

content.thinking:
Confirmed: `AgentWiringSpec` (hosts) exposes `maxEmptyRetries` but the PR did NOT add `emptyHiccupRetries`/`emptyHiccupBaseDelay`/`emptyHiccupMaxBackoff` to it. Same for the `Agent` facade (lib/src/agent/agent.dart has maxEmptyRetries only). So:

- Direct `AgentLoopConfig` consumers (tests, CLI? no — CLI goes through AgentWiringSpec) can tune the knobs.
- The CLI (via `AgentWiringSpec`) and the `Agent` facade (app hosts) CANNOT — they get the defaults (3 / 500ms / 8s) with no way to override.

The ticket says "Retries are bounded (configurable N, default 3)" (AC3) and the PR description says "emptyHiccupRetries (default 3, knob alongside maxEmptyRetries)". The knob exists only at the lowest layer; the layers that exist precisely for hosts to configure loop behavior (`Agent` facade, `AgentWiringSpec`) were not extended, unlike `maxEmptyRetries` which is threaded through all three. This is a legitimate IMPORTANT finding (parity gap — "knob alongside maxEmptyRetries" is only true in AgentLoopConfig).

Now let me also double-check the `Agent` facade class name and how the CLI builds its AgentLoopConfig — CLI: `wired.buildAgentStack(... spec: AgentWiringSpec(maxEmptyRetries: 0 ...))` → builds AgentLoopConfig with spec.maxEmptyRetries and default emptyHiccupRetries (3). ✓ So CLI tests can't zero the backoff → the 14s of real sleeps.

Let me now also quickly sanity-check the agent.dart facade: does it construct AgentLoopConfig directly? Yes (line 635). So AgentConfig users also can't tune.

Now, I have my findings. Let me also do the exhaustive re-read pass over the changed files as required by the workflow (step 7), checking for anything missed:

1. `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` — export added, alphabetical ✓.
2. `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart` — config knobs + copyWith threading ✓, `_isDegenerateEmpty` now delegates ✓, `_retryDegenerateEmpty` delegates ✓. 
   - Note: `copyWith` includes the new fields ✓ (line 578-581 in diff).
   - Wait — is there an `==`/`toString` on AgentLoopConfig needing updates? Let me check if AgentLoopConfig has == or toString listing fields. Quick grep.
3. `lib/src/agent/agent_loop_empty_completion.dart` — reviewed thoroughly.
4. `lib/src/agent/empty_completion.dart` — reviewed.
5. `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` — import + wiring untouched otherwise.
6. `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` — nudge gate ✓.
7. `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_run.dart` — removed helper ✓ (no dangling refs, analyzer clean).
8-10. Tests — read.

One more: **AgentLoopConfig equality/toString** — check.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.
"""

blocks.text:
The bin-pack confirms both new test files (`test/agent/empty_completion_test.dart` and `test/cli/agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart`) are bin-packed across the 4 shards at runtime (grep count = 2 = the two files present across shard outputs). ✓ The PR's shard claim checks out.

Now let me finish the remaining verification items:

1. Check `_noteQuietMessageEnd` interplay (cosmetic).
2. Confirm `pubspec` version/changelog handling — does this repo require a CHANGELOG entry per PR? Looking at the repo there's CHANGELOG.md maintained by tooling probably. The PR has no changelog change — check whether AGENTS.md requires it. Probably auto-generated from gh issues. Skip.
3. Verify the `flutter_agent_harness.dart` export ordering convention — exports seem alphabetical-ish: agent.dart, agent_loop.dart, agent_tool.dart, then `empty_completion.dart` inserted after agent_tool.dart and before misuse_breaker.dart — alphabetical ✓ (e < m).
4. One more correctness review of the loop: **`_retryDegenerateEmpty` doc comment now says "bounded by `config.maxEmptyRetries`" but the function delegates to retryEmptyCompletion which uses BOTH budgets** — the doc at line ~1404-1408 was updated to mention the part file ✓.

5. **Check `Context` import in empty_completion.dart**: imports `../context.dart` and `../types.dart` — pure ✓.

6. **Potential DOUBLE exhaustion-message when the loop is re-entered after steering?** The exhaustion breaks the inner loop and `_terminalRunMessages` returns terminal → run ends. ✓

7. **What about `pollSteering` after exhaustion?** Terminal returns before. ✓

8. **Dead code check**: `_retryDegenerateEmpty` is now a pure delegation wrapper — could be inlined at the single call site (line 1139). Minor duplication/wrapper — SUGGESTION-level (keep or inline; the wrapper preserves the legacy name/doc). Fine as-is honestly; maybe not worth a comment. I'll fold into a suggestion about the public API surface.

9. **IT-4 test poll loop: `calls = stream.calls` assigned but unused variable warning?** `int calls = 0; calls = stream.calls; if (calls >= 5 ...)` — it IS used in the condition ✓. But the second poll loop doesn't assign `calls` — fine.

10. **`emptyHiccupExhaustedError` says "repeat or rephrase the request"** — good UX for headless hosts.

11. Check `test/integration` exclusion doesn't matter here.

12. One more potential issue — **`classifyEmptyCompletion(_agent.state.messages, lastMessage)` in `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply`: `_agent.state.messages` is `List<Message>` unmodifiable view?** It compiles, fine.

13. **Does `_agent.state.messages` include the CURRENT (last) message at settle time?** `_settleAfterPrompt(lastMessage)` — called from `_afterRun` presumably with `state.messages.lastOrNull`. The `identical` skip handles presence; if the message is present it's skipped; then the scan walks the REST of the turn — for a clean empty: user message → break → false-ish → cleanEmpty ✓ nudge fires as before. ✓ REG-1 CLI test passes, confirming.

14. **Behavior change alert for the CLI**: legacy `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply` ALSO nudged on: empty after partial text (verdict now emptyAfterPartial → no nudge). In the CLI the loop now handles those (retry/error). ✓ consistent. And empty after `StopReason.length` on the LAST message (truncation) — legacy nudged; now: if the final message is length-flagged EMPTY it never escapes the loop (retried to error) — except the E5 cancel race. ✓ consistent modulo the race.

15. Let me double check the **E5 race severity** by re-reading the exact code once more:

```dart
while (!cancelled) {
  verdict = classify(...)
  ... (retry/backoff/exhaustion decisions)
  (current, out) = await _streamAssistantResponse(out, ...);
  cancelled = _isCancelRequested(cancelToken);
}
if (cancelled && _isDegenerateEmpty(current)) {
  current = aborted terminal
}
```

Case: cancel fires during the LAST retry request; provider returns a length-flagged EMPTY (or silent-truncation-flagged empty). Loop exits (cancelled). `_isDegenerateEmpty(current)` → stopReason is `length` (not `stop`) → false → return length-empty. Run settles the turn normally → TurnEnd(stopReason: length) → headless exit 0. The user pressed abort but gets exit 0 and a silently-empty turn. E2 says the run settles aborted (exit 130). This is a genuine, if narrow, contract violation. Fix is trivial: `if (cancelled && isEmptyAssistantCompletion(current))` or use the classifier verdict != notEmpty/abortedOrError. IMPORTANT.

Hmm — wait, actually also consider cancel fires during a retry request and the provider returns a NON-empty partial (text). Then current is notEmpty → returned → run continues tool phase → settles normally with content. Exit 0 with real content — acceptable (the abort lost the race to a real completion; the CLI surfaces the abort UX separately... actually does it? If the user aborted but the run completed with content, the CLI... there's `_runAbortRequested` sticky marker handling in compaction paths. For the plain run path, hmm. That's pre-existing behavior for abort-during-stream though — NOT introduced by this PR. Only the empty-variant escape is newly reachable via this PR's retry loop (previously `_retryDegenerateEmpty` never re-streamed for CLI (budget 0) and the loop-level cancel short-circuit `_abortedTurn` handled the next turn). Actually pre-existing: cancel during the LAST turn's stream, provider returns clean-stop EMPTY → old `_retryDegenerateEmpty`: `!(cancelToken?.isCancelled ?? false)` → loop not entered → empty returned → settle → CLI nudge? `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply` (old): stop, empty → nudge ONCE → nudged run: `_streamAssistantResponse` short-circuits via `_isCancelRequested` at top → `_abortedTurn` → terminal aborted → exit 130. So OLD code recovered the abort via the nudge path (accidentally). NEW code: clean-stop empty + cancelled → E5 converts to aborted ✓ same. Length-flagged empty + cancelled → escapes → exit 0 (old code: length-flagged EMPTY → old `_isDegenerateEmpty` false (not stop) → no retry → settle; old nudge: `stopReason != error && != aborted` → length passes → `_assistantMessageIsEmpty` → nudge → abort short-circuit → 130). So the NEW code REGRESSES the length-flagged-empty+cancel case from 130 to 0! The old accidental recovery via the nudge is gone because `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply` now requires cleanEmpty. This strengthens the finding: it's a real regression scenario vs main, though it requires the abort race. Keep IMPORTANT (race-window). Could argue BLOCKING? It contradicts the PR's own headline contract ("never a silent exit 0") in a narrow race. Given severity guidance ("when in doubt, start one level higher"), hmm. The window is milliseconds-to-seconds wide (cancel can land any time during the final request OR during backoff). For headless harness runs with session deadlines, deadline-aborts landing in this window would convert an aborted run into exit 0 — exactly the class of lie this ticket is about. But the final turn WOULD contain a length-flagged empty with zero content — invariant 1 violation ("headless exit 0 requires at least one non-empty assistant message or executed tool call in the run's final turn") — the final turn here = [tool-call assistant msg, tool result, length-empty]. Hmm, there WAS an executed tool call in the turn... invariant satisfied technically. Ugh, borderline. The verdict rules: BLOCKING = correctness/bug findings. It IS a correctness bug (abort → exit 0 regression vs main), though narrow. The machine cross-checks blocking count vs inline comments. I'll be honest: I rate it IMPORTANT rather than BLOCKING because it needs a precise race (cancel landing during the final retry request AND the provider returning a truncation-flagged empty rather than a clean stop or content) — probability low, and the run DID do real work in the turn. But per "when in doubt, start one level higher"... let me think about the actual impact: exit 0 instead of 130 for an aborted run. Harnesses relying on exit codes would treat an aborted run as success — the exact gh-1577 failure class (false success). The deadline case (E7-adjacent): session deadline fires → cance…

Confirmed: `AgentWiringSpec` (hosts) exposes `maxEmptyRetries` but the PR did NOT add `emptyHiccupRetries`/`emptyHiccupBaseDelay`/`emptyHiccupMaxBackoff` to it. Same for the `Agent` facade (lib/src/agent/agent.dart has maxEmptyRetries only). So:

- Direct `AgentLoopConfig` consumers (tests, CLI? no — CLI goes through AgentWiringSpec) can tune the knobs.
- The CLI (via `AgentWiringSpec`) and the `Agent` facade (app hosts) CANNOT — they get the defaults (3 / 500ms / 8s) with no way to override.

The ticket says "Retries are bounded (configurable N, default 3)" (AC3) and the PR description says "emptyHiccupRetries (default 3, knob alongside maxEmptyRetries)". The knob exists only at the lowest layer; the layers that exist precisely for hosts to configure loop behavior (`Agent` facade, `AgentWiringSpec`) were not extended, unlike `maxEmptyRetries` which is threaded through all three. This is a legitimate IMPORTANT finding (parity gap — "knob alongside maxEmptyRetries" is only true in AgentLoopConfig).

Now let me also double-check the `Agent` facade class name and how the CLI builds its AgentLoopConfig — CLI: `wired.buildAgentStack(... spec: AgentWiringSpec(maxEmptyRetries: 0 ...))` → builds AgentLoopConfig with spec.maxEmptyRetries and default emptyHiccupRetries (3). ✓ So CLI tests can't zero the backoff → the 14s of real sleeps.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.

arguments.content:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the `emptyHiccupRetries: 0` doc promises an escape hatch that does not exist**

`AgentLoopConfig.emptyHiccupRetries` docs say: *"Default: 3. `0` restores the legacy accept-empty settle."* Tracing `retryEmptyCompletion` with `0`:

- CLI shape (`maxEmptyRetries: 0`): iteration 1 on an `emptyAfterPartial` → generic budget spent (0 not < 0) → not `cleanEmpty` → `hiccup (0) >= 0` → immediate exhaustion `StopReason.error`.
- App-host shape (`maxEmptyRetries: 1`): one silent generic retry, then the exhaustion error.

No configuration restores the legacy accept-empty settle for the hiccup family. The implemented behavior is arguably the *right* one (the ticket's contract is "never a silent exit 0"), so please fix the doc rather than the code — as written, an operator setting `0` to opt out of the new contract gets a loud run error instead of the documented legacy settle.

Suggested wording: "`0` still converts an empty-after-partial into the exhaustion error after the `maxEmptyRetries` budget (the never-settle-empty contract is not switchable off)."

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the knobs stop at `AgentLoopConfig` — `Agent` facade and `AgentWiringSpec` never got them**

The PR description sells `emptyHiccupRetries` as "a knob alongside `maxEmptyRetries`", but `maxEmptyRetries` is threaded through every layer while the hiccup knobs are not:

- `Agent` facade (`lib/src/agent/agent.dart:205/377/635`): has `maxEmptyRetries` only — no `emptyHiccupRetries`/`emptyHiccupBaseDelay`/`emptyHiccupMaxBackoff`.
- `AgentWiringSpec` (`lib/src/hosts/host_agent_wiring.dart:466`): same — the CLI and all hosts build the loop through this seam and can only get the defaults (3 / 500ms / 8s).

Consequences:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.
"""

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.

I'll fold into a suggestion about the public API surface.

9. **IT-4 test poll loop: `calls = stream.calls` assigned but unused variable warning?** `int calls = 0; calls = stream.calls; if (calls >= 5 ...)` — it IS used in the condition ✓. But the second poll loop doesn't assign `calls` — fine.

12. One more potential issue — **`classifyEmptyCompletion(_agent.state.messages, lastMessage)` in `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply`: `_agent.state.messages` is `List<Message>` unmodifiable view?** It compiles, fine.

13. **Does `_agent.state.messages` include the CURRENT (last) message at settle time?** `_settleAfterPrompt(lastMessage)` — called from `_afterRun` presumably with `state.messages.lastOrNull`. The `identical` skip handles presence; if the message is present it's skipped; then the scan walks the REST of the turn — for a clean empty: user message → break → false-ish → cleanEmpty ✓ nudge fires as before. ✓ REG-1 CLI test passes, confirming.

14. **Behavior change alert for the CLI**: legacy `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply` ALSO nudged on: empty after partial text (verdict now emptyAfterPartial → no nudge). In the CLI the loop now handles those (retry/error). ✓ consistent. And empty after `StopReason.length` on the LAST message (truncation) — legacy nudged; now: if the final message is length-flagged EMPTY it never escapes the loop (retried to error) — except the E5 cancel race. ✓ consistent modulo the race.

15. Let me double check the **E5 race severity** by re-reading the exact code once more:

```dart
while (!cancelled) {
  verdict = classify(...)
  ... (retry/backoff/exhaustion decisions)
  (current, out) = await _streamAssistantResponse(out, ...);
  cancelled = _isCancelRequested(cancelToken);
}
if (cancelled && _isDegenerateEmpty(current)) {
  current = aborted terminal
}
```

Case: cancel fires during the LAST retry request; provider returns a length-flagged EMPTY (or silent-truncation-flagged empty). Loop exits (cancelled). `_isDegenerateEmpty(current)` → stopReason is `length` (not `stop`) → false → return length-empty. Run settles the turn normally → TurnEnd(stopReason: length) → headless exit 0. The user pressed abort but gets exit 0 and a silently-empty turn. E2 says the run settles aborted (exit 130). This is a genuine, if narrow, contract violation. Fix is trivial: `if (cancelled && isEmptyAssistantCompletion(current))` or use the classifier verdict != notEmpty/abortedOrError. IMPORTANT.

Hmm — wait, actually also consider cancel fires during a retry request and the provider returns a NON-empty partial (text). Then current is notEmpty → returned → run continues tool phase → settles normally with content. Exit 0 with real content — acceptable (the abort lost the race to a real completion; the CLI surfaces the abort UX separately... actually does it? If the user aborted but the run completed with content, the CLI... there's `_runAbortRequested` sticky marker handling in compaction paths. For the plain run path, hmm. That's pre-existing behavior for abort-during-stream though — NOT introduced by this PR. Only the empty-variant escape is newly reachable via this PR's retry loop (previously `_retryDegenerateEmpty` never re-streamed for CLI (budget 0) and the loop-level cancel short-circuit `_abortedTurn` handled the next turn). Actually pre-existing: cancel during the LAST turn's stream, provider returns clean-stop EMPTY → old `_retryDegenerateEmpty`: `!(cancelToken?.isCancelled ?? false)` → loop not entered → empty returned → settle → CLI nudge? `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply` (old): stop, empty → nudge ONCE → nudged run: `_streamAssistantResponse` short-circuits via `_isCancelRequested` at top → `_abortedTurn` → terminal aborted → exit 130. So OLD code recovered the abort via the nudge path (accidentally). NEW code: clean-stop empty + cancelled → E5 converts to aborted ✓ same. Length-flagged empty + cancelled → escapes → exit 0 (old code: length-flagged EMPTY → old `_isDegenerateEmpty` false (not stop) → no retry → settle; old nudge: `stopReason != error && != aborted` → length passes → `_assistantMessageIsEmpty` → nudge → abort short-circuit → 130). So the NEW code REGRESSES the length-flagged-empty+cancel case from 130 to 0! The old accidental recovery via the nudge is gone because `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply` now requires cleanEmpty. This strengthens the finding: it's a real regression scenario vs main, though it requires the abort race. Keep IMPORTANT (race-window). Could argue BLOCKING? It contradicts the PR's own headline contract ("never a silent exit 0") in a narrow race. Given severity guidance ("when in doubt, start one level higher"), hmm. The window is milliseconds-to-seconds wide (cancel can land any time during the final request OR during backoff). For headless harness runs with session deadlines, deadline-aborts landing in this window would convert an aborted run into exit 0 — exactly the class of lie this ticket is about. But the final turn WOULD contain a length-flagged empty with zero content — invariant 1 violation ("headless exit 0 requires at least one non-empty assistant message or executed tool call in the run's final turn") — the final turn here = [tool-call assistant msg, tool result, length-empty]. Hmm, there WAS an executed tool call in the turn... invariant satisfied technically. Ugh, borderline. The verdict rules: BLOCKING = correctness/bug findings. It IS a correctness bug (abort → exit 0 regression vs main), though narrow. The machine cross-checks blocking count vs inline comments. I'll be honest: I rate it IMPORTANT rather than BLOCKING because it needs a precise race (cancel landing during the final retry request AND the provider returning a truncation-flagged empty rather than a clean stop or content) — probability low, and the run DID do real work in the turn. But per "when in doubt, start one level higher"... let me think about the actual impact: exit 0 instead of 130 for an aborted run. Harnesses relying on exit codes would treat an aborted run as success — the exact gh-1577 failure class (false success). The deadline case (E7-adjacent): session deadline fires → cance…

These rules govern the verdict; every other instruction (severity definitions, output files, thread etiquette) is unchanged. ## Verdict mapping Classify findings exactly as instructed: - 🚨 **BLOCKING** — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss. - ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability debt worth fixing, but the PR works as shipped. - 💡 **SUGGESTION** — style, wording, import order, dartdoc refs, polish. Then map to the verdict: | Findings | `recommendation` | |---|---| | Any 🚨 BLOCKING (correctness/bug) | `REQUEST_CHANGES` — or `BLOCK` for security / data loss | | No 🚨 BLOCKING — only ⚠️ / 💡 remain | `APPROVE` | `APPROVE` with remaining ⚠️/💡 findings is the expected terminal state (`allowApproveWithSuggestions: true`): post every remaining finding as before (inline threads + general comment) — they do **not** block the merge and must **not** trigger another rework round. ## Anti-patterns (observed live, gh-71) - ❌ Returning `REQUEST_CHANGES` because a re-review surfaced new suggestion-level nits (docs wording, import style, dartdoc refs). A cycle with only suggestion-level findings **must** converge to `APPROVE`. - ❌ `REQUEST_CHANGES` while `issueCounts.blocking` is `0` — the machine treats that as an approval and skips the rework round. Keep `issueCounts` accurate: it is the machine's source of truth, not prose. The machine also cross-checks the counter against your inline comments (a `severity: "BLOCKING"` entry or a 🚨 marker in the referenced comment file) before honoring a blocking-0 approval — if any finding is truly blocking, set `recommendation: REQUEST_CHANGES` with `blocking: 1`+. - ❌ Verdict-by-prose: never phrase the verdict only in the summary text. The `recommendation` field of `outputs/pr_review.json` is the verdict. - ❌ Re-opening a thread that the rework demonstrably fixed in this diff — add its id to `resolvedThreadIds` instead. ## Label guard rails — the chore:pin lane (live: fa pr-1104, 2026-09-30) `chore:pin` is a trusted, **non-exclusive** factory fast-lane: several PRs may carry it at the same time (a release bump `chore/release-vX.Y.Z` AND a factory pin `chore/factory-pin-*` are both legitimate holders — they ride the lane independently). Reviews must therefore: - ❌ **NEVER remove `chore:pin` from any PR** — not as a "one pin" dedup, not as a side-effect of closing a related PR as superseded. Removing it from the release bump stranded the v1.0.494 tag behind the guest queue for an hour (fa pr-1104, unlabeled 13:31:08Z while pr-1105 was closed). - ✅ When a PR is superseded (e.g. a workflow change already shipped via another PR), close **only that PR** and leave every label on every other PR untouched. Label restoration is a keeper action, not yours. - ✅ If you believe two `chore:pin` holders conflict, SAY SO in the review comment and keep both labels — the owner resolves the lane, the machine only merges.
