# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1582
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1582
- **Title**: gh-1577 [GOAL] Empty completion after truncated stream is a retryable hiccup, never a silent exit 0 (B2)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1577` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1337
- **Deletions**: -69
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T10:03:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:35:51Z

## PR Description

Closes #1577
## gh-1577 — Empty completion after truncated stream is a retryable hiccup, never a silent exit 0

### What changed
- An empty assistant completion that follows partial content (assistant text, tool activity, or a truncation signal earlier in the turn) is now a **bounded-retry provider hiccup** in the agent loop; on retry exhaustion the run ends with a loud `StopReason.error` naming the hiccup, attempt count and last stop reason — headless `-p` exits 1, interactive prints the error and returns to the prompt. The silent exit-0 settle is gone.
- A clean empty (no partial content anywhere in the turn) keeps the #1085 M2b semantics exactly: one `continue` nudge per logical turn, then settle.

### Key decisions
- New pure classifier `classifyEmptyCompletion(turnHistory, message)` (`lib/src/agent/empty_completion.dart`) with verdicts `notEmpty` / `emptyAfterPartial` / `cleanEmpty` / `abortedOrError` — shared by the loop's retry machinery and the CLI's nudge gate; the partial-content window is the TURN (messages after the last user message), so an old truncation can never resurrect retries (E1).
- Truncation signals: `StopReason.length` plus the tolerated silent-truncation `errorMessage` flag count as partial-context evidence (E6); the `ToolCall` boundary survives — thinking-only turns with tool calls are never empty (AC6/E4).
- Retry policy lives in the loop (`agent_loop_empty_completion.dart`, a `part of agent_loop.dart` to stay under the 2800-line gate): `emptyHiccupRetries` (default 3, knob alongside `maxEmptyRetries`), exponential backoff in the model-roles `retry.baseDelayMs`/`maxBackoffMs` shape (500ms → 8s cap, deterministic), re-streamed through `_streamAssistantResponse`; retried empties stay in the transcript. `CancelToken` is honored between attempts; an abort racing the classification settles `aborted` (exit 130) — never the hiccup error, never a silent empty (E2/E5).
- Exhaustion reuses `StopReason.error` (open question 2) — the existing headless exit-code switch maps it to 1 with no switch change; the legacy `maxEmptyRetries` budget and the CLI's `maxEmptyRetries: 0` wiring are untouched.
- REG-2 scope note: the never-exit-0 contract is enforced for the hiccup family (empty after partial content) across the `stop` / length-flagged / silent-truncation-flagged paths; the clean-empty settle after its one nudge keeps AC2's pinned exit-0 behavior (REG-1).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/agent/empty_completion_test.dart test/agent/agent_loop_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart
dart test --exclude-tags integration   # full gate suite
```

### Test coverage
- UT-1..UT-5: classifier verdicts incl. thinking+ToolCall not empty, whitespace-only empty, backoff sequence.
- IT-1: `partial → empty → healthy` recovers and finishes (exit 0, retried empty in transcript). IT-2/E3: `partial → empty ×(N+1)` fires exactly N retries then the loud error. IT-3/REG-2: headless exhaustion exits 1 across all stop-reason variants. IT-4/AC5: interactive exhaustion returns to a steerable prompt. REG-1: clean-empty one-nudge tests unchanged.
- UT/IT run in the default CI shard (files verified bin-packed by `shard_files.py`); E2E-1 (live provider lane) and the REG required-check job wiring are CI-config follow-ups, no code dependency.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S[assistant completion] --> C{classifyEmptyCompletion}
  C -->|notEmpty / abortedOrError| OWN[existing terminal paths]
  C -->|cleanEmpty| NUDGE[one continue nudge, then settle - #1085 M2b unchanged]
  C -->|emptyAfterPartial| R[bounded retry: N=3, backoff 500ms to 8s]
  R -->|healthy| RUN[turn continues]
  R -->|cancel| AB[settle aborted - exit 130]
  R -->|N retries spent, still empty| ERR[StopReason.error naming hiccup + attempts + last stop]
  ERR -->|headless -p| X1[exit 1]
  ERR -->|interactive| P[error line + prompt stays alive]
```
</details>

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.

I'll fold into a suggestion about the public API surface.

9. **IT-4 test poll loop: `calls = stream.calls` assigned but unused variable warning?** `int calls = 0; calls = stream.calls; if (calls >= 5 ...)` — it IS used in the condition ✓. But the second poll loop doesn't assign `calls` — fine.

12. One more potential issue — **`classifyEmptyCompletion(_agent.state.messages, lastMessage)` in `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply`: `_agent.state.messages` is `List<Message>` unmodifiable view?** It compiles, fine.

13. **Does `_agent.state.messages` include the CURRENT (last) message at settle time?** `_settleAfterPrompt(lastMessage)` — called from `_afterRun` presumably with `state.messages.lastOrNull`. The `identical` skip handles presence; if the message is present it's skipped; then the scan walks the REST of the turn — for a clean empty: user message → break → false-ish → cleanEmpty ✓ nudge fires as before. ✓ REG-1 CLI test passes, confirming.

14. **Behavior change alert for the CLI**: legacy `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply` ALSO nudged on: empty after partial text (verdict now emptyAfterPartial → no nudge). In the CLI the loop now handles those (retry/error). ✓ consistent. And empty after `StopReason.length` on the LAST message (truncation) — legacy nudged; now: if the final message is length-flagged EMPTY it never escapes the loop (retried to error) — except the E5 cancel race. ✓ consistent modulo the race.

15. Let me double check the **E5 race severity** by re-reading the exact code once more:

```dart
while (!cancelled) {
  verdict = classify(...)
  ... (retry/backoff/exhaustion decisions)
  (current, out) = await _streamAssistantResponse(out, ...);
  cancelled = _isCancelRequested(cancelToken);
}
if (cancelled && _isDegenerateEmpty(current)) {
  current = aborted terminal
}
```

Case: cancel fires during the LAST retry request; provider returns a length-flagged EMPTY (or silent-truncation-flagged empty). Loop exits (cancelled). `_isDegenerateEmpty(current)` → stopReason is `length` (not `stop`) → false → return length-empty. Run settles the turn normally → TurnEnd(stopReason: length) → headless exit 0. The user pressed abort but gets exit 0 and a silently-empty turn. E2 says the run settles aborted (exit 130). This is a genuine, if narrow, contract violation. Fix is trivial: `if (cancelled && isEmptyAssistantCompletion(current))` or use the classifier verdict != notEmpty/abortedOrError. IMPORTANT.

Hmm — wait, actually also consider cancel fires during a retry request and the provider returns a NON-empty partial (text). Then current is notEmpty → returned → run continues tool phase → settles normally with content. Exit 0 with real content — acceptable (the abort lost the race to a real completion; the CLI surfaces the abort UX separately... actually does it? If the user aborted but the run completed with content, the CLI... there's `_runAbortRequested` sticky marker handling in compaction paths. For the plain run path, hmm. That's pre-existing behavior for abort-during-stream though — NOT introduced by this PR. Only the empty-variant escape is newly reachable via this PR's retry loop (previously `_retryDegenerateEmpty` never re-streamed for CLI (budget 0) and the loop-level cancel short-circuit `_abortedTurn` handled the next turn). Actually pre-existing: cancel during the LAST turn's stream, provider returns clean-stop EMPTY → old `_retryDegenerateEmpty`: `!(cancelToken?.isCancelled ?? false)` → loop not entered → empty returned → settle → CLI nudge? `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply` (old): stop, empty → nudge ONCE → nudged run: `_streamAssistantResponse` short-circuits via `_isCancelRequested` at top → `_abortedTurn` → terminal aborted → exit 130. So OLD code recovered the abort via the nudge path (accidentally). NEW code: clean-stop empty + cancelled → E5 converts to aborted ✓ same. Length-flagged empty + cancelled → escapes → exit 0 (old code: length-flagged EMPTY → old `_isDegenerateEmpty` false (not stop) → no retry → settle; old nudge: `stopReason != error && != aborted` → length passes → `_assistantMessageIsEmpty` → nudge → abort short-circuit → 130). So the NEW code REGRESSES the length-flagged-empty+cancel case from 130 to 0! The old accidental recovery via the nudge is gone because `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply` now requires cleanEmpty. This strengthens the finding: it's a real regression scenario vs main, though it requires the abort race. Keep IMPORTANT (race-window). Could argue BLOCKING? It contradicts the PR's own headline contract ("never a silent exit 0") in a narrow race. Given severity guidance ("when in doubt, start one level higher"), hmm. The window is milliseconds-to-seconds wide (cancel can land any time during the final request OR during backoff). For headless harness runs with session deadlines, deadline-aborts landing in this window would convert an aborted run into exit 0 — exactly the class of lie this ticket is about. But the final turn WOULD contain a length-flagged empty with zero content — invariant 1 violation ("headless exit 0 requires at least one non-empty assistant message or executed tool call in the run's final turn") — the final turn here = [tool-call assistant msg, tool result, length-empty]. Hmm, there WAS an executed tool call in the turn... invariant satisfied technically. Ugh, borderline. The verdict rules: BLOCKING = correctness/bug findings. It IS a correctness bug (abort → exit 0 regression vs main), though narrow. The machine cross-checks blocking count vs inline comments. I'll be honest: I rate it IMPORTANT rather than BLOCKING because it needs a precise race (cancel landing during the final retry request AND the provider returning a truncation-flagged empty rather than a clean stop or content) — probability low, and the run DID do real work in the turn. But per "when in doubt, start one level higher"... let me think about the actual impact: exit 0 instead of 130 for an aborted run. Harnesses relying on exit codes would treat an aborted run as success — the exact gh-1577 failure class (false success). The deadline case (E7-adjacent): session deadline fires → cance…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1582
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1582
- **Title**: gh-1577 [GOAL] Empty completion after truncated stream is a retryable hiccup, never a silent exit 0 (B2)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1577` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1337
- **Deletions**: -69
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T10:03:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:35:51Z

## PR Description

Closes #1577
## gh-1577 — Empty completion after truncated stream is a retryable hiccup, never a silent exit 0

### What changed
- An empty assistant completion that follows partial content (assistant text, tool activity, or a truncation signal earlier in the turn) is now a **bounded-retry provider hiccup** in the agent loop; on retry exhaustion the run ends with a loud `StopReason.error` naming the hiccup, attempt count and last stop reason — headless `-p` exits 1, interactive prints the error and returns to the prompt. The silent exit-0 settle is gone.
- A clean empty (no partial content anywhere in the turn) keeps the #1085 M2b semantics exactly: one `continue` nudge per logical turn, then settle.

### Key decisions
- New pure classifier `classifyEmptyCompletion(turnHistory, message)` (`lib/src/agent/empty_completion.dart`) with verdicts `notEmpty` / `emptyAfterPartial` / `cleanEmpty` / `abortedOrError` — shared by the loop's retry machinery and the CLI's nudge gate; the partial-content window is the TURN (messages after the last user message), so an old truncation can never resurrect retries (E1).
- Truncation signals: `StopReason.length` plus the tolerated silent-truncation `errorMessage` flag count as partial-context evidence (E6); the `ToolCall` boundary survives — thinking-only turns with tool calls are never empty (AC6/E4).
- Retry policy lives in the loop (`agent_loop_empty_completion.dart`, a `part of agent_loop.dart` to stay under the 2800-line gate): `emptyHiccupRetries` (default 3, knob alongside `maxEmptyRetries`), exponential backoff in the model-roles `retry.baseDelayMs`/`maxBackoffMs` shape (500ms → 8s cap, deterministic), re-streamed through `_streamAssistantResponse`; retried empties stay in the transcript. `CancelToken` is honored between attempts; an abort racing the classification settles `aborted` (exit 130) — never the hiccup error, never a silent empty (E2/E5).
- Exhaustion reuses `StopReason.error` (open question 2) — the existing headless exit-code switch maps it to 1 with no switch change; the legacy `maxEmptyRetries` budget and the CLI's `maxEmptyRetries: 0` wiring are untouched.
- REG-2 scope note: the never-exit-0 contract is enforced for the hiccup family (empty after partial content) across the `stop` / length-flagged / silent-truncation-flagged paths; the clean-empty settle after its one nudge keeps AC2's pinned exit-0 behavior (REG-1).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/agent/empty_completion_test.dart test/agent/agent_loop_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart
dart test --exclude-tags integration   # full gate suite
```

### Test coverage
- UT-1..UT-5: classifier verdicts incl. thinking+ToolCall not empty, whitespace-only empty, backoff sequence.
- IT-1: `partial → empty → healthy` recovers and finishes (exit 0, retried empty in transcript). IT-2/E3: `partial → empty ×(N+1)` fires exactly N retries then the loud error. IT-3/REG-2: headless exhaustion exits 1 across all stop-reason variants. IT-4/AC5: interactive exhaustion returns to a steerable prompt. REG-1: clean-empty one-nudge tests unchanged.
- UT/IT run in the default CI shard (files verified bin-packed by `shard_files.py`); E2E-1 (live provider lane) and the REG required-check job wiring are CI-config follow-ups, no code dependency.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S[assistant completion] --> C{classifyEmptyCompletion}
  C -->|notEmpty / abortedOrError| OWN[existing terminal paths]
  C -->|cleanEmpty| NUDGE[one continue nudge, then settle - #1085 M2b unchanged]
  C -->|emptyAfterPartial| R[bounded retry: N=3, backoff 500ms to 8s]
  R -->|healthy| RUN[turn continues]
  R -->|cancel| AB[settle aborted - exit 130]
  R -->|N retries spent, still empty| ERR[StopReason.error naming hiccup + attempts + last stop]
  ERR -->|headless -p| X1[exit 1]
  ERR -->|interactive| P[error line + prompt stays alive]
```
</details>

# Note: n_0997_f1c6

flutter_agent_harness gotcha (gh-1577 rework, pr-1582): the agent loop consumes the AssistantMessage's OWN stopReason — DoneEvent.reason is never merged into the message (DoneEvent.partial => message). Scripted provider turns that model "length"-flagged or otherwise cut-off completions must set stopReason on the MESSAGE (testAssistant(stopReason: StopReason.length)), not just DoneEvent(reason: length). Several pre-existing fixtures (agent_loop_test.dart lengthEmptyTurn, agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart REG-2 lengthEmpty) had it wrong and were silently exercising clean-stop empties. Also: AssistantMessageEventStream consumers return at the terminal event (DoneEvent/ErrorEvent) WITHOUT waiting for stream.end() — holding end() does not hold a scripted request in flight; to model a cancel-racing-request, serve only a non-terminal StartEvent and push the terminal from cancelToken.onCancel.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1582
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1582
- **Title**: gh-1577 [GOAL] Empty completion after truncated stream is a retryable hiccup, never a silent exit 0 (B2)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1577` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1337
- **Deletions**: -69
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T10:03:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:35:51Z

## PR Description

Closes #1577
## gh-1577 — Empty completion after truncated stream is a retryable hiccup, never a silent exit 0

### What changed
- An empty assistant completion that follows partial content (assistant text, tool activity, or a truncation signal earlier in the turn) is now a **bounded-retry provider hiccup** in the agent loop; on retry exhaustion the run ends with a loud `StopReason.error` naming the hiccup, attempt count and last stop reason — headless `-p` exits 1, interactive prints the error and returns to the prompt. The silent exit-0 settle is gone.
- A clean empty (no partial content anywhere in the turn) keeps the #1085 M2b semantics exactly: one `continue` nudge per logical turn, then settle.

### Key decisions
- New pure classifier `classifyEmptyCompletion(turnHistory, message)` (`lib/src/agent/empty_completion.dart`) with verdicts `notEmpty` / `emptyAfterPartial` / `cleanEmpty` / `abortedOrError` — shared by the loop's retry machinery and the CLI's nudge gate; the partial-content window is the TURN (messages after the last user message), so an old truncation can never resurrect retries (E1).
- Truncation signals: `StopReason.length` plus the tolerated silent-truncation `errorMessage` flag count as partial-context evidence (E6); the `ToolCall` boundary survives — thinking-only turns with tool calls are never empty (AC6/E4).
- Retry policy lives in the loop (`agent_loop_empty_completion.dart`, a `part of agent_loop.dart` to stay under the 2800-line gate): `emptyHiccupRetries` (default 3, knob alongside `maxEmptyRetries`), exponential backoff in the model-roles `retry.baseDelayMs`/`maxBackoffMs` shape (500ms → 8s cap, deterministic), re-streamed through `_streamAssistantResponse`; retried empties stay in the transcript. `CancelToken` is honored between attempts; an abort racing the classification settles `aborted` (exit 130) — never the hiccup error, never a silent empty (E2/E5).
- Exhaustion reuses `StopReason.error` (open question 2) — the existing headless exit-code switch maps it to 1 with no switch change; the legacy `maxEmptyRetries` budget and the CLI's `maxEmptyRetries: 0` wiring are untouched.
- REG-2 scope note: the never-exit-0 contract is enforced for the hiccup family (empty after partial content) across the `stop` / length-flagged / silent-truncation-flagged paths; the clean-empty settle after its one nudge keeps AC2's pinned exit-0 behavior (REG-1).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/agent/empty_completion_test.dart test/agent/agent_loop_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart
dart test --exclude-tags integration   # full gate suite
```

### Test coverage
- UT-1..UT-5: classifier verdicts incl. thinking+ToolCall not empty, whitespace-only empty, backoff sequence.
- IT-1: `partial → empty → healthy` recovers and finishes (exit 0, retried empty in transcript). IT-2/E3: `partial → empty ×(N+1)` fires exactly N retries then the loud error. IT-3/REG-2: headless exhaustion exits 1 across all stop-reason variants. IT-4/AC5: interactive exhaustion returns to a steerable prompt. REG-1: clean-empty one-nudge tests unchanged.
- UT/IT run in the default CI shard (files verified bin-packed by `shard_files.py`); E2E-1 (live provider lane) and the REG required-check job wiring are CI-config follow-ups, no code dependency.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S[assistant completion] --> C{classifyEmptyCompletion}
  C -->|notEmpty / abortedOrError| OWN[existing terminal paths]
  C -->|cleanEmpty| NUDGE[one continue nudge, then settle - #1085 M2b unchanged]
  C -->|emptyAfterPartial| R[bounded retry: N=3, backoff 500ms to 8s]
  R -->|healthy| RUN[turn continues]
  R -->|cancel| AB[settle aborted - exit 130]
  R -->|N retries spent, still empty| ERR[StopReason.error naming hiccup + attempts + last stop]
  ERR -->|headless -p| X1[exit 1]
  ERR -->|interactive| P[error line + prompt stays alive]
```
</details>

# Note: n_0997_f1c6

flutter_agent_harness gotcha (gh-1577 rework, pr-1582): the agent loop consumes the AssistantMessage's OWN stopReason — DoneEvent.reason is never merged into the message (DoneEvent.partial => message). Scripted provider turns that model "length"-flagged or otherwise cut-off completions must set stopReason on the MESSAGE (testAssistant(stopReason: StopReason.length)), not just DoneEvent(reason: length). Several pre-existing fixtures (agent_loop_test.dart lengthEmptyTurn, agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart REG-2 lengthEmpty) had it wrong and were silently exercising clean-stop empties. Also: AssistantMessageEventStream consumers return at the terminal event (DoneEvent/ErrorEvent) WITHOUT waiting for stream.end() — holding end() does not hold a scripted request in flight; to model a cancel-racing-request, serve only a non-terminal StartEvent and push the terminal from cancelToken.onCancel.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1582
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1582
- **Title**: gh-1577 [GOAL] Empty completion after truncated stream is a retryable hiccup, never a silent exit 0 (B2)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1577` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1337
- **Deletions**: -69
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T10:03:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:35:51Z

## PR Description

Closes #1577
## gh-1577 — Empty completion after truncated stream is a retryable hiccup, never a silent exit 0

### What changed
- An empty assistant completion that follows partial content (assistant text, tool activity, or a truncation signal earlier in the turn) is now a **bounded-retry provider hiccup** in the agent loop; on retry exhaustion the run ends with a loud `StopReason.error` naming the hiccup, attempt count and last stop reason — headless `-p` exits 1, interactive prints the error and returns to the prompt. The silent exit-0 settle is gone.
- A clean empty (no partial content anywhere in the turn) keeps the #1085 M2b semantics exactly: one `continue` nudge per logical turn, then settle.

### Key decisions
- New pure classifier `classifyEmptyCompletion(turnHistory, message)` (`lib/src/agent/empty_completion.dart`) with verdicts `notEmpty` / `emptyAfterPartial` / `cleanEmpty` / `abortedOrError` — shared by the loop's retry machinery and the CLI's nudge gate; the partial-content window is the TURN (messages after the last user message), so an old truncation can never resurrect retries (E1).
- Truncation signals: `StopReason.length` plus the tolerated silent-truncation `errorMessage` flag count as partial-context evidence (E6); the `ToolCall` boundary survives — thinking-only turns with tool calls are never empty (AC6/E4).
- Retry policy lives in the loop (`agent_loop_empty_completion.dart`, a `part of agent_loop.dart` to stay under the 2800-line gate): `emptyHiccupRetries` (default 3, knob alongside `maxEmptyRetries`), exponential backoff in the model-roles `retry.baseDelayMs`/`maxBackoffMs` shape (500ms → 8s cap, deterministic), re-streamed through `_streamAssistantResponse`; retried empties stay in the transcript. `CancelToken` is honored between attempts; an abort racing the classification settles `aborted` (exit 130) — never the hiccup error, never a silent empty (E2/E5).
- Exhaustion reuses `StopReason.error` (open question 2) — the existing headless exit-code switch maps it to 1 with no switch change; the legacy `maxEmptyRetries` budget and the CLI's `maxEmptyRetries: 0` wiring are untouched.
- REG-2 scope note: the never-exit-0 contract is enforced for the hiccup family (empty after partial content) across the `stop` / length-flagged / silent-truncation-flagged paths; the clean-empty settle after its one nudge keeps AC2's pinned exit-0 behavior (REG-1).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/agent/empty_completion_test.dart test/agent/agent_loop_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart
dart test --exclude-tags integration   # full gate suite
```

### Test coverage
- UT-1..UT-5: classifier verdicts incl. thinking+ToolCall not empty, whitespace-only empty, backoff sequence.
- IT-1: `partial → empty → healthy` recovers and finishes (exit 0, retried empty in transcript). IT-2/E3: `partial → empty ×(N+1)` fires exactly N retries then the loud error. IT-3/REG-2: headless exhaustion exits 1 across all stop-reason variants. IT-4/AC5: interactive exhaustion returns to a steerable prompt. REG-1: clean-empty one-nudge tests unchanged.
- UT/IT run in the default CI shard (files verified bin-packed by `shard_files.py`); E2E-1 (live provider lane) and the REG required-check job wiring are CI-config follow-ups, no code dependency.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S[assistant completion] --> C{classifyEmptyCompletion}
  C -->|notEmpty / abortedOrError| OWN[existing terminal paths]
  C -->|cleanEmpty| NUDGE[one continue nudge, then settle - #1085 M2b unchanged]
  C -->|emptyAfterPartial| R[bounded retry: N=3, backoff 500ms to 8s]
  R -->|healthy| RUN[turn continues]
  R -->|cancel| AB[settle aborted - exit 130]
  R -->|N retries spent, still empty| ERR[StopReason.error naming hiccup + attempts + last stop]
  ERR -->|headless -p| X1[exit 1]
  ERR -->|interactive| P[error line + prompt stays alive]
```
</details>

# Note: n_0997_f1c6

flutter_agent_harness gotcha (gh-1577 rework, pr-1582): the agent loop consumes the AssistantMessage's OWN stopReason — DoneEvent.reason is never merged into the message (DoneEvent.partial => message). Scripted provider turns that model "length"-flagged or otherwise cut-off completions must set stopReason on the MESSAGE (testAssistant(stopReason: StopReason.length)), not just DoneEvent(reason: length). Several pre-existing fixtures (agent_loop_test.dart lengthEmptyTurn, agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart REG-2 lengthEmpty) had it wrong and were silently exercising clean-stop empties. Also: AssistantMessageEventStream consumers return at the terminal event (DoneEvent/ErrorEvent) WITHOUT waiting for stream.end() — holding end() does not hold a scripted request in flight; to model a cancel-racing-request, serve only a non-terminal StartEvent and push the terminal from cancelToken.onCancel.

`FakeStreamFunction.turns` uses `removeAt(0)` — MUTATES the list! In the REG-2 test:

```dart
final lengthEmpty = [DoneEvent(...)];
final silentTruncationEmpty = [DoneEvent(...)];
for (final scripted in [lengthEmpty, silentTruncationEmpty]) {
  final stream = FakeStreamFunction([
    truncatedToolCallTurn,
    scripted,
    scripted,
    scripted,
    scripted,
  ]);
```

The outer list literal `[truncatedToolCallTurn, scripted, scripted, scripted, scripted]` contains FOUR REFERENCES to the SAME inner list `scripted`. `FakeStreamFunction` calls `turns.removeAt(0)` on the OUTER list — that removes the reference from the outer list, not the inner list's contents. The inner list `scripted` is only iterated (`for (final event in turns.removeAt(0))`) — never mutated. So the same scripted turn replays 4 times fine. ✓ No bug.

But wait — `truncatedToolCallTurn` is a field initialized once per test... it's `final truncatedToolCallTurn = toolTurn([...])` at main() level, reused across tests in REG-2 — again only iterated. ✓.

Hmm, but note: in the IT tests, `turns.removeAt(0)` will throw RangeError if the loop makes more requests than scripted turns — a de-facto assertion. Fine.

Now — real-time backoff in CLI tests: `cliFor` doesn't override `emptyHiccupBaseDelay` (and can't — AgentCliConfig doesn't expose it... let me verify: the CLI builds AgentWiringSpec without emptyHiccup knobs, so tests use the DEFAULT 500ms/8s. IT-2: 500+1000+2000 = 3.5s. REG-2: 2 variants × 3.5s = 7s. IT-4: 3.5s. Total ≈ 14s of wall-clock sleep in this one test file. Plus the 25ms-poll loops. This slows the default CI shard. The agent_loop_test.dart tests override `emptyHiccupBaseDelay: Duration.zero` ✓ (cliShapeConfig). So only the CLI tests sleep. Worth a SUGGESTION (or IMPORTANT given this repo's gate obsession with CI times?). I'll rate SUGGESTION — it's ~14s.

Hmm, actually — for the CLI tests to override the delay, AgentCliConfig would need the knob wired through AgentWiringSpec → AgentLoopConfig. The wiring doesn't exist (CLI always uses default 3/500ms/8s). That's also a review point: **the CLI cannot configure the hiccup knobs** — the ticket says "configurable N, default 3" — configurable at the library config level. The CLI reads no env/flag for it. The ticket's capability table says "Bounded backoff retry (headless -p) | yes | default N=3, configurable". Library-level configurable satisfies it loosely. I'd note it as a SUGGESTION (wire the knob through AgentWiringSpec so hosts/CLI can tune; also enables tests to zero the backoff).

Now, the more significant issues to verify:

**Issue A (IMPORTANT/BLOCKING?): `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply` double-nudge regression risk.** Legacy: any non-error/aborted empty got the nudge (including empty-after-partial, empty-after-length). New: ONLY cleanEmpty gets the nudge. Consider a scenario in the INTERACTIVE CLI: user's turn → model streams partial text (truncated, length) → loop retries 3× → recovers or errors. Fine. But what about a scenario where the LOOP isn't involved: the nudge path calls `_runPrompt('continue', isAutoContinue: true)` — the nudged run itself has the loop inside, so empties after partial are handled by the loop. Consistent.

BUT — here's a subtle one: after the hiccup retries RECOVER (a healthy completion lands), all good. After EXHAUSTION, the final message is StopReason.error → `_settleAfterPrompt` first branch → not CodeMie, not over-window → `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply(error message)` → classifier: abortedOrError → false → return true → run finishes with the error → headless exit 1 ✓, interactive prints error line ✓.

What about a length-flagged empty that does NOT enter the hiccup path? Can that happen? In the loop, every empty (except error/aborted) is classified; length-flagged empty IS emptyAfterPartial → retried. So the only empty messages escaping the loop are: notEmpty, cleanEmpty (after budgets), aborted, error. The CLI nudge only fires on cleanEmpty ✓. A length-empty can escape ONLY via the E5 cancel race noted above.

**Issue B: `emptyHiccupRetries: 0` doc comment claims "restores the legacy accept-empty settle" but actually converts empty-after-partial into an immediate exhaustion error (with CLI's maxEmptyRetries=0, zero retries).** For the APP host (maxEmptyRetries=1): generic retry 1 without backoff, then exhaustion. So "0 restores legacy settle" is wrong in both wirings. Doc-only, but it's public API doc on a new config knob — IMPORTANT? It misleads operators into thinking they can opt out of the new never-exit-0 contract. Given the whole point of the ticket is "never a silent exit 0", an operator setting 0 expecting legacy behavior gets a loud error instead. That's arguably BETTER but the doc lies. I'd rate IMPORTANT (public API doc inaccuracy on a knob whose semantics matter). Hmm, or SUGGESTION. The verdict rules: IMPORTANT = "real maintainability debt worth fixing, but the PR works as shipped". Doc inaccuracy on a new public knob = IMPORTANT-ish. I'll go IMPORTANT.

But consider: model returns empty with error stop mid-retry → abortedOrError → break → terminal error path ✓. Consider: empty (cleanEmpty verdict — no partial in turn) with host budget: generic=1 retry, still cleanEmpty → break → CLI nudges once. Legacy: `_retryDegenerateEmpty` retried once for degenerate empty → same ✓.

BUT here's a subtle behavior difference in the loop for the APP HOST with cleanEmpty: legacy retried `while degenerate && retries < maxEmptyRetries` — i.e., if retry 1 also empty → stop retrying (retries=1 == max) → return empty → settle. New: same (generic=1 → break on cleanEmpty). ✓ identical.

**Issue F: `classifyEmptyCompletion` in `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply` — O(turn) scan per settle, trivial. Fine.

**Issue G: The `_turnCarriesPartialContent` scan skips `message` via `identical` but ONLY the first match.** If `message` appears earlier in history (impossible — messages are unique objects) fine. But what if `message` is NOT in `turnHistory`? `sawMessage` stays false; the scan just processes from the end — correct behavior anyway.

Wait, actually there's a subtle bug here: `if (!sawMessage && identical(entry, message)) { sawMessage = true; continue; }` — this skips the message itself only the FIRST time it's seen from the end. If `message` IS the last element (normal case), the scan starts after it ✓. What if the same message object appears... no, impossible.

Hmm, but consider: the loop calls `classifyEmptyCompletion(out.messages, current)` — `out.messages` includes ALL prior retries' empty messages. Those are skipped for partial-evidence (empty, no truncation signal → continue scanning) — correct: an empty doesn't count as partial content, but ALSO doesn't stop the scan. So after 3 empties, the scan still reaches the original partial text → stays emptyAfterPartial ✓ (matches IT-2: all 4 empties classify emptyAfterPartial).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1582
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1582
- **Title**: gh-1577 [GOAL] Empty completion after truncated stream is a retryable hiccup, never a silent exit 0 (B2)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1577` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1337
- **Deletions**: -69
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T10:03:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:35:51Z

## PR Description

Closes #1577
## gh-1577 — Empty completion after truncated stream is a retryable hiccup, never a silent exit 0

### What changed
- An empty assistant completion that follows partial content (assistant text, tool activity, or a truncation signal earlier in the turn) is now a **bounded-retry provider hiccup** in the agent loop; on retry exhaustion the run ends with a loud `StopReason.error` naming the hiccup, attempt count and last stop reason — headless `-p` exits 1, interactive prints the error and returns to the prompt. The silent exit-0 settle is gone.
- A clean empty (no partial content anywhere in the turn) keeps the #1085 M2b semantics exactly: one `continue` nudge per logical turn, then settle.

### Key decisions
- New pure classifier `classifyEmptyCompletion(turnHistory, message)` (`lib/src/agent/empty_completion.dart`) with verdicts `notEmpty` / `emptyAfterPartial` / `cleanEmpty` / `abortedOrError` — shared by the loop's retry machinery and the CLI's nudge gate; the partial-content window is the TURN (messages after the last user message), so an old truncation can never resurrect retries (E1).
- Truncation signals: `StopReason.length` plus the tolerated silent-truncation `errorMessage` flag count as partial-context evidence (E6); the `ToolCall` boundary survives — thinking-only turns with tool calls are never empty (AC6/E4).
- Retry policy lives in the loop (`agent_loop_empty_completion.dart`, a `part of agent_loop.dart` to stay under the 2800-line gate): `emptyHiccupRetries` (default 3, knob alongside `maxEmptyRetries`), exponential backoff in the model-roles `retry.baseDelayMs`/`maxBackoffMs` shape (500ms → 8s cap, deterministic), re-streamed through `_streamAssistantResponse`; retried empties stay in the transcript. `CancelToken` is honored between attempts; an abort racing the classification settles `aborted` (exit 130) — never the hiccup error, never a silent empty (E2/E5).
- Exhaustion reuses `StopReason.error` (open question 2) — the existing headless exit-code switch maps it to 1 with no switch change; the legacy `maxEmptyRetries` budget and the CLI's `maxEmptyRetries: 0` wiring are untouched.
- REG-2 scope note: the never-exit-0 contract is enforced for the hiccup family (empty after partial content) across the `stop` / length-flagged / silent-truncation-flagged paths; the clean-empty settle after its one nudge keeps AC2's pinned exit-0 behavior (REG-1).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/agent/empty_completion_test.dart test/agent/agent_loop_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart
dart test --exclude-tags integration   # full gate suite
```

### Test coverage
- UT-1..UT-5: classifier verdicts incl. thinking+ToolCall not empty, whitespace-only empty, backoff sequence.
- IT-1: `partial → empty → healthy` recovers and finishes (exit 0, retried empty in transcript). IT-2/E3: `partial → empty ×(N+1)` fires exactly N retries then the loud error. IT-3/REG-2: headless exhaustion exits 1 across all stop-reason variants. IT-4/AC5: interactive exhaustion returns to a steerable prompt. REG-1: clean-empty one-nudge tests unchanged.
- UT/IT run in the default CI shard (files verified bin-packed by `shard_files.py`); E2E-1 (live provider lane) and the REG required-check job wiring are CI-config follow-ups, no code dependency.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S[assistant completion] --> C{classifyEmptyCompletion}
  C -->|notEmpty / abortedOrError| OWN[existing terminal paths]
  C -->|cleanEmpty| NUDGE[one continue nudge, then settle - #1085 M2b unchanged]
  C -->|emptyAfterPartial| R[bounded retry: N=3, backoff 500ms to 8s]
  R -->|healthy| RUN[turn continues]
  R -->|cancel| AB[settle aborted - exit 130]
  R -->|N retries spent, still empty| ERR[StopReason.error naming hiccup + attempts + last stop]
  ERR -->|headless -p| X1[exit 1]
  ERR -->|interactive| P[error line + prompt stays alive]
```
</details>

# Note: n_0997_f1c6

flutter_agent_harness gotcha (gh-1577 rework, pr-1582): the agent loop consumes the AssistantMessage's OWN stopReason — DoneEvent.reason is never merged into the message (DoneEvent.partial => message). Scripted provider turns that model "length"-flagged or otherwise cut-off completions must set stopReason on the MESSAGE (testAssistant(stopReason: StopReason.length)), not just DoneEvent(reason: length). Several pre-existing fixtures (agent_loop_test.dart lengthEmptyTurn, agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart REG-2 lengthEmpty) had it wrong and were silently exercising clean-stop empties. Also: AssistantMessageEventStream consumers return at the terminal event (DoneEvent/ErrorEvent) WITHOUT waiting for stream.end() — holding end() does not hold a scripted request in flight; to model a cancel-racing-request, serve only a non-terminal StartEvent and push the terminal from cancelToken.onCancel.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1582
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1582
- **Title**: gh-1577 [GOAL] Empty completion after truncated stream is a retryable hiccup, never a silent exit 0 (B2)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1577` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1337
- **Deletions**: -69
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T10:03:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:35:51Z

## PR Description

Closes #1577
## gh-1577 — Empty completion after truncated stream is a retryable hiccup, never a silent exit 0

### What changed
- An empty assistant completion that follows partial content (assistant text, tool activity, or a truncation signal earlier in the turn) is now a **bounded-retry provider hiccup** in the agent loop; on retry exhaustion the run ends with a loud `StopReason.error` naming the hiccup, attempt count and last stop reason — headless `-p` exits 1, interactive prints the error and returns to the prompt. The silent exit-0 settle is gone.
- A clean empty (no partial content anywhere in the turn) keeps the #1085 M2b semantics exactly: one `continue` nudge per logical turn, then settle.

### Key decisions
- New pure classifier `classifyEmptyCompletion(turnHistory, message)` (`lib/src/agent/empty_completion.dart`) with verdicts `notEmpty` / `emptyAfterPartial` / `cleanEmpty` / `abortedOrError` — shared by the loop's retry machinery and the CLI's nudge gate; the partial-content window is the TURN (messages after the last user message), so an old truncation can never resurrect retries (E1).
- Truncation signals: `StopReason.length` plus the tolerated silent-truncation `errorMessage` flag count as partial-context evidence (E6); the `ToolCall` boundary survives — thinking-only turns with tool calls are never empty (AC6/E4).
- Retry policy lives in the loop (`agent_loop_empty_completion.dart`, a `part of agent_loop.dart` to stay under the 2800-line gate): `emptyHiccupRetries` (default 3, knob alongside `maxEmptyRetries`), exponential backoff in the model-roles `retry.baseDelayMs`/`maxBackoffMs` shape (500ms → 8s cap, deterministic), re-streamed through `_streamAssistantResponse`; retried empties stay in the transcript. `CancelToken` is honored between attempts; an abort racing the classification settles `aborted` (exit 130) — never the hiccup error, never a silent empty (E2/E5).
- Exhaustion reuses `StopReason.error` (open question 2) — the existing headless exit-code switch maps it to 1 with no switch change; the legacy `maxEmptyRetries` budget and the CLI's `maxEmptyRetries: 0` wiring are untouched.
- REG-2 scope note: the never-exit-0 contract is enforced for the hiccup family (empty after partial content) across the `stop` / length-flagged / silent-truncation-flagged paths; the clean-empty settle after its one nudge keeps AC2's pinned exit-0 behavior (REG-1).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/agent/empty_completion_test.dart test/agent/agent_loop_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart
dart test --exclude-tags integration   # full gate suite
```

### Test coverage
- UT-1..UT-5: classifier verdicts incl. thinking+ToolCall not empty, whitespace-only empty, backoff sequence.
- IT-1: `partial → empty → healthy` recovers and finishes (exit 0, retried empty in transcript). IT-2/E3: `partial → empty ×(N+1)` fires exactly N retries then the loud error. IT-3/REG-2: headless exhaustion exits 1 across all stop-reason variants. IT-4/AC5: interactive exhaustion returns to a steerable prompt. REG-1: clean-empty one-nudge tests unchanged.
- UT/IT run in the default CI shard (files verified bin-packed by `shard_files.py`); E2E-1 (live provider lane) and the REG required-check job wiring are CI-config follow-ups, no code dependency.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S[assistant completion] --> C{classifyEmptyCompletion}
  C -->|notEmpty / abortedOrError| OWN[existing terminal paths]
  C -->|cleanEmpty| NUDGE[one continue nudge, then settle - #1085 M2b unchanged]
  C -->|emptyAfterPartial| R[bounded retry: N=3, backoff 500ms to 8s]
  R -->|healthy| RUN[turn continues]
  R -->|cancel| AB[settle aborted - exit 130]
  R -->|N retries spent, still empty| ERR[StopReason.error naming hiccup + attempts + last stop]
  ERR -->|headless -p| X1[exit 1]
  ERR -->|interactive| P[error line + prompt stays alive]
```
</details>

1. BLOCKING E5 abort conversion → widened to `isEmptyAssistantCompletion` with `!= StopReason.aborted` term
2. Doc fix for `emptyHiccupRetries: 0`
3. Knob threading through `Agent` facade / `AgentWiringSpec` / `AgentCliConfig`
4. Cancellation-aware backoff via `Future.any`

Also important note from the rework: they discovered `DoneEvent(reason: StopReason.length, ...)` is NOT merged into the message — the loop consumes the message's own stopReason. They corrected earlier fixtures. Interesting — that affects the REG-2 test in the ORIGINAL diff which used `DoneEvent(reason: StopReason.length, message: testAssistant())` — those fixtures were corrected.

- Re-opening a thread that the rework demonstrably fixed in this diff → add its id to resolvedThreadIds.
- Verify each fix genuinely landed and is correct.
- Surface any NEW findings (but only BLOCKING/IMPORTANT can justify REQUEST_CHANGES; suggestion-only → APPROVE).

3. Verify each of the 4 fixes:
   a. E5 post-loop guard: `cancelled && current.stopReason != StopReason.aborted && isEmptyAssistantCompletion(current)`. Check correctness: does it introduce any NEW issue? E.g., cancelled + error-stop empty → converted to aborted — "abort wins" fine. Note: `isEmptyAssistantCompletion` doesn't check stop reason, so aborted-empty also matches, but the `!= aborted` term excludes it. What about the exhaustion terminal message (error + empty)? It's set then `break` — post-check runs with stale `cancelled`... if cancelled was set true after the last stream and before exhaustion — wait: exhaustion path only reached when `cancelled` false at loop top... Actually exhaustion branch runs inside the loop while `!cancelled`; `cancelled` only updates after `_streamAssistantResponse`. If cancel fires DURING the final `_streamAssistantResponse` (which returned the last empty), then `cancelled=true` → loop exits → post-check converts. But exhaustion check happens at loop TOP before streaming — sequence: verdict emptyAfterPartial, hiccup exhausted → set error terminal → break → post-check: `cancelled` (from previous stream) false → no convert ✓. If cancel fired during the last stream, loop exits before exhaustion check ✓. OK.
   
   One more: with the widened guard, consider cancel firing after a HEALTHY (non-empty) final response — `isEmptyAssistantCompletion` false → no convert → normal settle. Fine (abort lost the race to real content).
   
   And cancel + error-stop empty (provider error): converted to aborted — exit 130 instead of 1; "abort wins" per E5; acceptable and arguably correct.

   b. Doc fix — read the new wording.
   c. Knob threading — read agent.dart, host_agent_wiring.dart, agent_cli_config.dart, agent_cli.dart changes. Check defaults (3/500ms/8s) and no breaking changes to constructors (named optional params with defaults → backward compatible).
   d. Future.any backoff — check implementation + the `cancelToken.onCancel` future. Note: `Future.any` with a never-completing delayed future and onCancel completing → fine. One subtlety: `Future<void>.delayed(delay)` keeps a timer alive even if onCancel wins the race — the timer still fires later but result discarded. Fine.

4. If the OLD REG-2 fixtures (DoneEvent(reason: length, message: testAssistant())) never produced a length-flagged message, then the original REG-2 test was testing clean-stop empties (mislabeled). id: "n_0997_f1c6"
type: "note"
title: "flutter_agent_harness gotcha (gh-1577 rework, pr-1582): the agent loop consumes the AssistantMessage's OWN stopReason — DoneEvent.reason is never merged into the message (DoneEvent.partial => message). Scripted provider turns that model \"length\"-flagged or otherwise cut-off completions must set stopReason on the MESSAGE (testAssistant(stopReason: StopReason.length)), not just DoneEvent(reason: length). Several pre-existing fixtures (agent_loop_test.dart lengthEmptyTurn, agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart REG-2 lengthEmpty) had it wrong and were silently exercising clean-stop empties. Also: AssistantMessageEventStream consumers return at the terminal event (DoneEvent/ErrorEvent) WITHOUT waiting for stream.end() — holding end() does not hold a scripted request in flight; to model a cancel-racing-request, serve only a non-terminal StartEvent and push the terminal from cancelToken.onCancel."

# Note: n_0997_f1c6

flutter_agent_harness gotcha (gh-1577 rework, pr-1582): the agent loop consumes the AssistantMessage's OWN stopReason — DoneEvent.reason is never merged into the message (DoneEvent.partial => message). Scripted provider turns that model "length"-flagged or otherwise cut-off completions must set stopReason on the MESSAGE (testAssistant(stopReason: StopReason.length)), not just DoneEvent(reason: length). Several pre-existing fixtures (agent_loop_test.dart lengthEmptyTurn, agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart REG-2 lengthEmpty) had it wrong and were silently exercising clean-stop empties. Also: AssistantMessageEventStream consumers return at the terminal event (DoneEvent/ErrorEvent) WITHOUT waiting for stream.end() — holding end() does not hold a scripted request in flight; to model a cancel-racing-request, serve only a non-terminal StartEvent and push the terminal from cancelToken.onCancel.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.

The `identical` skip handles presence; if the message is present it's skipped; then the scan walks the REST of the turn — for a clean empty: user message → break → false-ish → cleanEmpty ✓ nudge fires as before. ✓ REG-1 CLI test passes, confirming.

And empty after `StopReason.length` on the LAST message (truncation) — legacy nudged; now: if the final message is length-flagged EMPTY it never escapes the loop (retried to error) — except the E5 cancel race. ✓ consistent modulo the race.

15. Let me double check the **E5 race severity** by re-reading the exact code once more:

```dart
while (!cancelled) {
  verdict = classify(...)
  ... (retry/backoff/exhaustion decisions)
  (current, out) = await _streamAssistantResponse(out, ...);
  cancelled = _isCancelRequested(cancelToken);
}
if (cancelled && _isDegenerateEmpty(current)) {
  current = aborted terminal
}
```

Case: cancel fires during the LAST retry request; provider returns a length-flagged EMPTY (or silent-truncation-flagged empty). Loop exits (cancelled). `_isDegenerateEmpty(current)` → stopReason is `length` (not `stop`) → false → return length-empty. Run settles the turn normally → TurnEnd(stopReason: length) → headless exit 0. The user pressed abort but gets exit 0 and a silently-empty turn. E2 says the run settles aborted (exit 130). This is a genuine, if narrow, contract violation. Fix is trivial: `if (cancelled && isEmptyAssistantCompletion(current))` or use the classifier verdict != notEmpty/abortedOrError. IMPORTANT.

Hmm — wait, actually also consider cancel fires during a retry request and the provider returns a NON-empty partial (text). Then current is notEmpty → returned → run continues tool phase → settles normally with content. Exit 0 with real content — acceptable (the abort lost the race to a real completion; the CLI surfaces the abort UX separately... actually does it? If the user aborted but the run completed with content, the CLI... there's `_runAbortRequested` sticky marker handling in compaction paths. For the plain run path, hmm. That's pre-existing behavior for abort-during-stream though — NOT introduced by this PR. Only the empty-variant escape is newly reachable via this PR's retry loop (previously `_retryDegenerateEmpty` never re-streamed for CLI (budget 0) and the loop-level cancel short-circuit `_abortedTurn` handled the next turn). Actually pre-existing: cancel during the LAST turn's stream, provider returns clean-stop EMPTY → old `_retryDegenerateEmpty`: `!(cancelToken?.isCancelled ?? false)` → loop not entered → empty returned → settle → CLI nudge? `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply` (old): stop, empty → nudge ONCE → nudged run: `_streamAssistantResponse` short-circuits via `_isCancelRequested` at top → `_abortedTurn` → terminal aborted → exit 130. So OLD code recovered the abort via the nudge path (accidentally). NEW code: clean-stop empty + cancelled → E5 converts to aborted ✓ same. Length-flagged empty + cancelled → escapes → exit 0 (old code: length-flagged EMPTY → old `_isDegenerateEmpty` false (not stop) → no retry → settle; old nudge: `stopReason != error && != aborted` → length passes → `_assistantMessageIsEmpty` → nudge → abort short-circuit → 130). So the NEW code REGRESSES the length-flagged-empty+cancel case from 130 to 0! The old accidental recovery via the nudge is gone because `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply` now requires cleanEmpty. This strengthens the finding: it's a real regression scenario vs main, though it requires the abort race. Keep IMPORTANT (race-window). Could argue BLOCKING? It contradicts the PR's own headline contract ("never a silent exit 0") in a narrow race. Given severity guidance ("when in doubt, start one level higher"), hmm. The window is milliseconds-to-seconds wide (cancel can land any time during the final request OR during backoff). For headless harness runs with session deadlines, deadline-aborts landing in this window would convert an aborted run into exit 0 — exactly the class of lie this ticket is about. But the final turn WOULD contain a length-flagged empty with zero content — invariant 1 violation ("headless exit 0 requires at least one non-empty assistant message or executed tool call in the run's final turn") — the final turn here = [tool-call assistant msg, tool result, length-empty]. Hmm, there WAS an executed tool call in the turn... invariant satisfied technically. Ugh, borderline. The verdict rules: BLOCKING = correctness/bug findings. It IS a correctness bug (abort → exit 0 regression vs main), though narrow. The machine cross-checks blocking count vs inline comments. I'll be honest: I rate it IMPORTANT rather than BLOCKING because it needs a precise race (cancel landing during the final retry request AND the provider returning a truncation-flagged empty rather than a clean stop or content) — probability low, and the run DID do real work in the turn. But per "when in doubt, start one level higher"... let me think about the actual impact: exit 0 instead of 130 for an aborted run. Harnesses relying on exit codes would treat an aborted run as success — the exact gh-1577 failure class (false success). The deadline case (E7-adjacent): session deadline fires → cance…

Findings summary:
1. **BLOCKING** — `agent_loop_empty_completion.dart:89`: E5 abort-race conversion only covers clean-stop empties (`_isDegenerateEmpty` requires `StopReason.stop`). Cancel/deadline abort landing while the final retry request returns a length-flagged or silent-truncation-flagged empty → the empty escapes the loop as a final message → run settles as a normal turn → headless exit 0 on an aborted run. Regression vs main: the old nudge path (`stopReason != error && != aborted && empty` → nudge → `_streamAssistantResponse` cancel short-circuit → aborted/130) used to catch these. One-line fix: convert ANY empty (`isEmptyAssistantCompletion`) when cancelled, e.g. `if (cancelled && isEmptyAssistantCompletion(current))`.

Severity check: this is a correctness finding where abort can still yield exit 0 with an empty final completion — the exact bug class gh-1577 targets → BLOCKING → REQUEST_CHANGES. issueCounts.blocking = 1. Consistent machine protocol: recommendation REQUEST_CHANGES with blocking ≥ 1 ✓.

2. **IMPORTANT** — `agent_loop.dart:490`: doc "`0` restores the legacy accept-empty settle" is wrong: with 0 and `maxEmptyRetries: 0` (CLI shape) the first empty-after-partial goes straight to the exhaustion error; with the app default `maxEmptyRetries: 1` it's 1 silent retry then the error. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1582
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1582
- **Title**: gh-1577 [GOAL] Empty completion after truncated stream is a retryable hiccup, never a silent exit 0 (B2)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1577` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1337
- **Deletions**: -69
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T10:03:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:35:51Z

## PR Description

Closes #1577
## gh-1577 — Empty completion after truncated stream is a retryable hiccup, never a silent exit 0

### What changed
- An empty assistant completion that follows partial content (assistant text, tool activity, or a truncation signal earlier in the turn) is now a **bounded-retry provider hiccup** in the agent loop; on retry exhaustion the run ends with a loud `StopReason.error` naming the hiccup, attempt count and last stop reason — headless `-p` exits 1, interactive prints the error and returns to the prompt. The silent exit-0 settle is gone.
- A clean empty (no partial content anywhere in the turn) keeps the #1085 M2b semantics exactly: one `continue` nudge per logical turn, then settle.

### Key decisions
- New pure classifier `classifyEmptyCompletion(turnHistory, message)` (`lib/src/agent/empty_completion.dart`) with verdicts `notEmpty` / `emptyAfterPartial` / `cleanEmpty` / `abortedOrError` — shared by the loop's retry machinery and the CLI's nudge gate; the partial-content window is the TURN (messages after the last user message), so an old truncation can never resurrect retries (E1).
- Truncation signals: `StopReason.length` plus the tolerated silent-truncation `errorMessage` flag count as partial-context evidence (E6); the `ToolCall` boundary survives — thinking-only turns with tool calls are never empty (AC6/E4).
- Retry policy lives in the loop (`agent_loop_empty_completion.dart`, a `part of agent_loop.dart` to stay under the 2800-line gate): `emptyHiccupRetries` (default 3, knob alongside `maxEmptyRetries`), exponential backoff in the model-roles `retry.baseDelayMs`/`maxBackoffMs` shape (500ms → 8s cap, deterministic), re-streamed through `_streamAssistantResponse`; retried empties stay in the transcript. `CancelToken` is honored between attempts; an abort racing the classification settles `aborted` (exit 130) — never the hiccup error, never a silent empty (E2/E5).
- Exhaustion reuses `StopReason.error` (open question 2) — the existing headless exit-code switch maps it to 1 with no switch change; the legacy `maxEmptyRetries` budget and the CLI's `maxEmptyRetries: 0` wiring are untouched.
- REG-2 scope note: the never-exit-0 contract is enforced for the hiccup family (empty after partial content) across the `stop` / length-flagged / silent-truncation-flagged paths; the clean-empty settle after its one nudge keeps AC2's pinned exit-0 behavior (REG-1).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/agent/empty_completion_test.dart test/agent/agent_loop_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart
dart test --exclude-tags integration   # full gate suite
```

### Test coverage
- UT-1..UT-5: classifier verdicts incl. thinking+ToolCall not empty, whitespace-only empty, backoff sequence.
- IT-1: `partial → empty → healthy` recovers and finishes (exit 0, retried empty in transcript). IT-2/E3: `partial → empty ×(N+1)` fires exactly N retries then the loud error. IT-3/REG-2: headless exhaustion exits 1 across all stop-reason variants. IT-4/AC5: interactive exhaustion returns to a steerable prompt. REG-1: clean-empty one-nudge tests unchanged.
- UT/IT run in the default CI shard (files verified bin-packed by `shard_files.py`); E2E-1 (live provider lane) and the REG required-check job wiring are CI-config follow-ups, no code dependency.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S[assistant completion] --> C{classifyEmptyCompletion}
  C -->|notEmpty / abortedOrError| OWN[existing terminal paths]
  C -->|cleanEmpty| NUDGE[one continue nudge, then settle - #1085 M2b unchanged]
  C -->|emptyAfterPartial| R[bounded retry: N=3, backoff 500ms to 8s]
  R -->|healthy| RUN[turn continues]
  R -->|cancel| AB[settle aborted - exit 130]
  R -->|N retries spent, still empty| ERR[StopReason.error naming hiccup + attempts + last stop]
  ERR -->|headless -p| X1[exit 1]
  ERR -->|interactive| P[error line + prompt stays alive]
```
</details>

# Note: n_0997_f1c6

flutter_agent_harness gotcha (gh-1577 rework, pr-1582): the agent loop consumes the AssistantMessage's OWN stopReason — DoneEvent.reason is never merged into the message (DoneEvent.partial => message). Scripted provider turns that model "length"-flagged or otherwise cut-off completions must set stopReason on the MESSAGE (testAssistant(stopReason: StopReason.length)), not just DoneEvent(reason: length). Several pre-existing fixtures (agent_loop_test.dart lengthEmptyTurn, agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart REG-2 lengthEmpty) had it wrong and were silently exercising clean-stop empties. Also: AssistantMessageEventStream consumers return at the terminal event (DoneEvent/ErrorEvent) WITHOUT waiting for stream.end() — holding end() does not hold a scripted request in flight; to model a cancel-racing-request, serve only a non-terminal StartEvent and push the terminal from cancelToken.onCancel.

**By:** [[agent]]
**Date:** 2026-10-13T19:10:08.430903Z
**Area:** [[project|project]]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.

Now let me finish the remaining verification items:

1. Check `_noteQuietMessageEnd` interplay (cosmetic).
2. Confirm `pubspec` version/changelog handling — does this repo require a CHANGELOG entry per PR? Looking at the repo there's CHANGELOG.md maintained by tooling probably. The PR has no changelog change — check whether AGENTS.md requires it. Probably auto-generated from gh issues. Skip.
